item.title: Creating with Pastels with Becky Holden
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded: In this class, students will have the chance to explore the many facets of working with pastels. Becky will introduce concepts using demonstrations and examples from modern and historic works of art. The course lessons are designed to help build art skills while learning new pastel techniques. There will be art critiques, and individual instruction. Whether you’re new to pastels or an experienced pastel artist, this class is sure to challenge and excite you. Becky’s been painting in pastels for years and has a lot to share.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:

  • Kneaded Eraser

    • Medium Pastels: Rembrandt
    • Soft Pastels: Sennelier

item.title: Stacked Squares with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded: Great for beginners and advanced students, this workshop will teach cutting skills and the proper ways to stack glass in a variety of sizes and colors for a perfectly fused one of a kind dish or bowl. Learn how the different thicknesses and layout of the glass will form in the kiln and the proper fusing schedules that will be used to bring it all together!

item.title: Mornings with Manon with Manon Sander
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded:
Learn how to capture the landscape en plein air while infusing your painting with luminous light. Manon will share her secrets to tackle a scene through simple shapes, correct values, mixing of accurate color, and impressionistic paint application. Demos and short lectures combined with plenty of fun painting time with Manon's help will accelerate and fine-tune your painting skills. Suitable for oils, acrylics, gouache. acceptable. Working knowledge of your medium and basic drawing skills beneficial.
Winter: Members Only: $381 Class Dates: 1/8, 1/15, 1/22, 1/29, 2/12, 2/19, 2/26

*Please call the gallery to register: 561-746-3101

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
Manon’s List of Suggested Materials

Paints

Titanium White (for travel I prefer Gamblin Quick Dry) Lemon Yellow or Cadmium Yellow Light Cadmium Yellow Medium   Indian Yellow   Cadmium Orange or Permanent Orange (Michael Harding) Yellow Ochre or Golden Ochre Cadmium Red Light or Naphtol Red Quinacridone Red/Rose or Permanent Alizarin Crimson Phthalo Blue or Cerulean Ultramarine Blue Viridian or Pthalo Green Transparent Red Oxide or Indian Red Ivory Black  I prefer Michael Harding or Gamblin Artist Oils. The colors printed boldly are the ones I like to use. Michael Harding has put my own paint set together with 10 of my favorite colors. It is available through me on request. The set is $190. In general, as long as you have a warm and a cool version of yellow, blue, and red you should be good to go, but I recommend using artist grade paints, not student or artisan grade, which usually have less pigment.

Medium

  • Gamsol. Please no turpentine or other smelly solvents!
  • Gamblin Galkyd Lite

Brushes

As long as you have a variety of long flats and filberts you’ll be good. Rosemary Shiraz and Ivory are my favorite brushes. Please no short stubby brushes or old stiff paint-encrusted brushes. I love my Rosemary Shiraz and Ivory in the following sizes:
  • Size 1 round
  • Size 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 long-bristled flats
Optional:
  • One skinny rigger brush for fine lines
  • 2" diamond-shaped palette knife (I also love my ½" palette knife for color mixing)
Rosemary has put together my own brush set. It contains 13 brushes, mostly long flats and a few other fun ones. It is $106 and is available through me on request.

Canvas

Small(ish) canvas panels, such as 6x8", 8x10", 9x12". Personally, I prefer to paint on linen panels by Centurion or Fredrix. For travel, Canva Plein Air ArtBoard is a lightweight option.

Miscellaneous

  • Paper towels (blue shop towels from Home Depot are great). I cut my roll in half to save space in my bag. (Don’t try this with a serrated knife.)
  • Small sketchbook and pencil. I also recommend 3 value markers in light, medium, and dark. You can get them for about $6 at Walmart. I like to use them with my little Crescent sketchbook because its paper won’t let the markers bleed through.
  • Easel, tripod, palette
  • Plastic bags for your trash
  • Container for your mineral spirits
  • Sunscreen
  • Hat or visor
  • Bug spray
  • Rain protection
  • Wet canvas carrier (I like Panelpak)
  • Water, snack
  • Optional: Umbrella and stool

item.title: Intro to Jewelry & Metalsmithing with Ace Tilton Ratcliff (Thursday)
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded:
Students will be introduced to the fundamentals of metalsmithing through instructor demonstrations, one-on-one instruction, and hands-on experience with hand tools, flex shafts, and torches. Each student will learn to design, pierce, drill, solder, and set a cabochon stone. Students will work with sterling silver, brass, and copper throughout this course and projects will include making rings, pendants, and/or earrings. Sterling silver, copper, and saw blades are available for purchase in the studio from your instructor. Please see the student material list for prices and descriptions.
No class Nov. 6

  • Herkules White Label #2/0 Saw Blade 1 dozen

  • Sterling Silver 1/4” Strip, 16-Ga., Dead-Soft 3”
*We will discuss purchasing a round or oval cabochon stone for this class. You are welcome to bring one you already have, just make sure it is no smaller than 10mm.

item.title: Strung with Elegance: Pearl Knotting Basics with Tracey Roedl
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded: Create your own freshwater cultured pearl bracelet with a sterling silver clasp! Students will learn the proper technique of pearl stringing and knotting using sterling french wire, diamond drill bits, and silk cord. You can also use this technique to repair any broken strands you might have. All materials are included.

item.title: Building Skills in Painting with Tina Kraft
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded:
“Art is Long, and life is short”- Hippocrates
Participants will learn the building blocks of painting while strengthening their artistic vision and skills. The essential use of drawing, mixing color and painting techniques are demonstrated in each class. Fundamentals using the notan sketch, limited palettes of color and color relationships, compositional elements like scale, ranging from big to small, structure in the rectangle and the use of the grid will be presented. Referencing images of great paintings from art history will guide our develop of ideas. Individuals are encouraged to explore their personal interests through experimentation and creativity! Beginners to painting are welcome.

item.title: Glass Under Construction with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded: Build a house out of glass!!! In this one-day workshop, you will learn how to draw and lay out your plans for the construction of a glass house. Students use the basic glass fusion techniques for cutting glass as well as learn how to use a ring saw to cut out tiny patterns in glass. Using a wide variety of accessory glass, glass line paints, and more you will decorate your new home and fuse it together with copper wiring....roof, and all! Please wear closed toes shoes, comfortable clothes, and an apron. Bring your lunch or we can have it ordered in.

item.title: Fused Glass Draped Vases with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded:
Get ready for spring with beautiful, fused glass free standing and wall vases! This 4-week class will introduce you to the beauty of using heat and gravity to create a graceful look in glass. Students will learn how to cut circles to build your glass cutting and kiln forming skills to create one-of-a-kind art glass pieces to add to your collection or give as a gift to others. Previous glass cutting skills recommended. Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase.
Closed-toed shoes are a requirement.
Email Carolyn@LighthouseArts.org with any questions

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Spring; Members Only $420 (April 2, April 9, April 16, and April 23)

item.title: Keum-Boo with Marsha Levey Blandy
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded: In this workshop, we will use an ancient Korean gilding technique, Keum-boo, that applies thin sheets of gold (23.5k) to argentium for a beautiful finish. This is the perfect way to achieve using gold on your work without the expense of solid gold. Fused instead of soldered, students will make a pendant or pair of earrings. Students will learn how to apply Keum-boo on a flat using both a torch and flat top burner. Your tuition covers all gold materials and argentium to make it easy and affordable. All levels are welcome and will be successful! Those with more experience will be able to push the boundaries of their projects. (Registration Deadline: Monday, April 1st)

item.title: Inventive Silver Clay with Marthe Harwell
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded: Silver metal clay (also known as Precious Metal Clay) is a clay material created by mixing microscopic particles of pure silver in an organic matrix (binder) with water that can be shaped into infinite designs to create unique fine silver jewelry.  Using molds and tools to create shapes and impressions, the clay is then fired at a high temperature to burn off the binder, revealing a finished fine silver product.  During this workshop, we will use a variety of clay products using the appropriate tools to produce unique jewelry.  If you have explored working with polymer clay and regular clay, you will be delighted to work with silver clay to create your original designs of jewelry. All materials are included with your tuition!

item.title: Silver Clay & Glass Pendants with Carolyn Austin and Marthe Harwell
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded: In this 2-day workshop, students will learn how to make pendants using fused glass cabochons and silver clay that they create and fuse. Day 1:  Students will explore how heat and gravity are used to develop round or other shaped cabochons for jewelry.  Students will learn glass-cutting skills and have a wide variety of glass and glass accessories. Day 2: Students we will make their one-of-a-kind silver clay pendant using a variety of application methods to set their fused glass cabochon. Silver clay comes in both a syringe and traditional solid lump form allowing for a range of effects once fired in the kiln. All materials are included with your tuition!

item.title: Streaky Glass Creations with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded: Specialty production manufactured glass comes in many beautiful designs...almost too pretty to change. In this 3-hour workshop, you will be challenged to do just that! Choosing from a variety of streaky glass you will be dared to cut it up and learn the countless possibilities to designing and transforming the pieces to create your own pattern into a one-of-a-kind functional piece of glass art. Materials and firing schedules are included with additional materials and firings schedules available for purchase. Please wear closed-toed shoes, comfortable clothes, and an apron.

item.title: Bas Relief: Low Relief in Clay with Eduardo Gomez
item.dc:creator: Jlicata
item.content:encoded: Use your mark making techniques on clay and learn the secrets of combining your drawing and sculpting skills to make bas relief sculpture (aka low relief). Each student is asked to provide source imagery for sculpting for example; photo of a family dog or an interesting magazine clip of a garden. Images should be around 8 ½ by 11 in. Within the class structure we will look at and discuss some famous bas relief artworks and how they used foreshortening/perspective successfully. No previous sculpture experience required, but some drawing proficiency is recommended. This Workshop includes 25lbs of low fire clay and one firing.

item.title: Molding and Cold Cast your Bas Relief with Eduardo Gomez
item.dc:creator: Jlicata
item.content:encoded: Important notice **recommended to take previous workshop or have a relief prepared** This workshop will teach students the process of making a single part mold to cast. Each student will become familiar with the materials used for mold making, and pouring materials as urethane resin and bronze powder. This practice will result in a relief which looks like a bronze casting but is cheaper and light enough for hanging. All students who have a relief are encouraged to take this class. The previous relief sculptures can be fired or it can be green (not bisqued) as long as the piece is at least leather hard.

item.title: Sculpting the Human Head : Portrait with Eduardo Gomez
item.dc:creator: Jlicata
item.content:encoded:
The workshop will cover basic anatomy of the head and anatomical proportions. It will also cover anatomical issues related to aging and race and facial expressions. It will teach students how to use the shape and the planes of the face to obtain a general likeness. We will also study different ways of modeling the individual parts such as the nose, lips, ears and eyes. Certain surface finishing techniques will also be covered.
The class will also cover basic design issues involved in designing a bust sculpture as well as how to prepare it for firing or molding, and different mounting options. Workshop includes 25lbs of low fire clay and one bisque firing.

item.title: Lilly Pulitzer Canvas Painting with Melissa Sixma Lingo
item.dc:creator: Jlicata
item.content:encoded: Create your own Lilly Pulitzer inspired masterpiece! Learn tips and tricks that will free your inner Bohemian Queen. Lilly Pulitzer was a rule-breaker who knew “style isn’t just about what you wear, it’s about how you live.” The Lilly Pulitzer brand’s in-house print studio carries their founder’s spirit close to their hearts when the print artists paint each original print design. Workshop guests will receive first-hand tips and tricks for painting a floral canvas from a print expert, learn how to gain confidence in their painting abilities, how to mix Lilly-inspired colors and stick to a premixed palette, and how to compose various types of content inspired by natural plant and animal life...with room for whimsy and a wink!

item.title: Fun with Gouache with Manon Sander
item.dc:creator: Jlicata
item.content:encoded: In this fun workshop you will get introduced to using this exciting water-based medium properly, so you can enjoy its portability on your travels or at home. Get acquainted with gouache’s unique properties while you create small paintings from your own photographs. Manon will go over materials, demo how to handle gouache, create a charming little gouache painting in simple steps, and help you with your own paintings. Gouaches are a great medium for small frameable paintings and travel sketchbooks. Fun With Gouache Supply List

item.title: Double the Contrast - Black and White Abstract Painting with Mixed Media with Lisa Macnamara
item.dc:creator: Jlicata
item.content:encoded: High contrasts/drama with black and white - Creating an abstract painting using these 2 colors or 2 colors of your choice take an object apart, deconstruct it visually creating something new Experimenting with tape to create negative space and paper materials There is freedom to try something out of your regular painting parameters! Does it have to be on canvas? Bring in an object like a vase and let’s make it something new using the Black and White abstract techniques.

item.title: Build a Glass House with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: Jlicata
item.content:encoded:
Build a house out of glass!!! In this 4 week class you will learn how to draw and lay out your plans for the construction of a glass house...beach house, traditional or a Barnhouse...whatever style you may like! Students will learn and use the basic glass fusion techniques for cutting glass as well as learn how to use a wide variety of accessory glass, glass line paints and more to decorate and accessorize your new home. Students will then learn how to fuse it together using fiber paper and copper wiring....roof and all! Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase.
Please wear close-toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.
Email Carolyn Austin with any question at Caroly@lighthousearts.org

item.title: Painting Seascapes and Waves with Olena Babak
item.dc:creator: Jlicata
item.content:encoded: Day 1: Dive into the art of painting realistic transparent water and rolling waves. The lesson commences with a drawing demonstration, delving into the wave's structure. Students will follow along with their own drawings. Subsequently, the instructor will apply the drawing exercise's lessons in a painting demonstration, with students replicating on their canvases. Individual critiques from the instructor will be provided throughout the day, using oil paints as the preferred medium. Day 2: Head to the beach as students transition studio lessons into painting from life. Throughout the day, the instructor offers individual critiques, ensuring a seamless application of skills in an outdoor setting.   Painting Seascapes & Waves Supply List

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Day 1: 373 Tequesta Dr. - Studio C ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀ Day 2: Offsite
Plein Air Workshop with Olena Babak

item.title: Create Your Own Sheet of Glass with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Why would you work with ordinary manufacturers sheet glass when you can create your own part sheets to design a one of a kind decorative or functional piece of glass art. Students will learn about glass compatibility, firing schedules and how glass behaves in the kiln. Explore the many options and designs that can be achieved by using a wide variety of techniques and tools with frit, stringers and glass powders. Once the part sheets are fired they will then be deconstructed to be used for reconstruction of a truly one of a kind design to be fired again. Students will then learn how to prepare molds for the slumping of their final art piece.
Please wear closed- toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron if you like.
Materials and firing schedules are included with additional materials and firings schedules available for purchase. Email Carolyn with any questions at :Carolyn@lighthousearts.org

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Late Spring; Members Only $315 (May 7, May 14, and May 21)

item.title: Fused Glass Sun Catchers or Coasters with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded: Great for Beginners and a fun night out with friends and family! Try your hand at Glass Fusion. In this mini-workshop, you will learn how to assemble and properly lay out a pattern using a variety of colored glass, frit, and stingers to create a one-of-a-kind decorative sun catcher or coaster in a comfortable relaxed atmosphere. Students 12-18 years of age require a guardian 21 years of age plus. Please wear closed-toed shoes, comfortable clothes, and an apron if you like. All materials and firings included.

item.title: Paint Your Travels & Memories with Eileen Lyons
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Many of us travel, whether real or imagined. Learn how to document your travels through watercolor and colored pencil on a small scale. Explore techniques, methods, and materials to pack in your suitcase for your next adventure. Photography is an excellent way to document your journey, however, painting or drawing a place deepens the experience. Learn how to paint moments from previous/future trips or paint your way into a dream trip. Using memories and captured moments, participants will paint and draw from photos in the studio, en plein air (outside), and will ultimately create a collection of small works in a book, telling a travel story.

item.title: The Golden Hour and Sunset with Carl Bretzke
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded:
The objective of this workshop is to learn the nature of late afternoon and sunset “light effects” and then develop an efficient method to capture that effect in paint. The techniques for capturing The Golden Hour Light Effect will be demonstrated through the use of a PowerPoint presentation, live mini-demos, and then supervised individual painting sessions. For this workshop, you should bring all of your usual painting gear. A nocturne light is strongly recommended so that you can more easily see during our sunset painting session. I recommend preloading your palettes with paint to save time.
The Golden Hour and Sunset Supply List

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Plein Air Workshop with Carl Bretzke

item.title: Relax with Art - For the Caregiver with Danica Papali
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded:
This class is designed to help the Caregiver shift focus from the care of others and learn to declare through artistic practice. The goal of this workshop will be to begin an art journal. Participants will use Neuerographica and grounding techniques to explore and express emotions through the art-making process.
The focus of the class will be on the process of art creation. There is no need to have any prior art skill or knowledge. This class is appropriate for the absolute beginner, or any artist interested in learning to use art to connect to personal insights and wellbeing. The class provides but is not limited to acrylic, watercolor, pastel, drawing tools, and other media.
Get to know your local museum in an interactive museum tour, while learning a working knowledge of basic art principles and how to use basic art terminology.

item.title: Night Out at the Museum with Danica Papali
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded:
The class will start with an art scavenger hunt, using art terms, and definitions. The scavenger hunt activity will be followed by an art project time where the group will have an opportunity to try unique, beginner art activities. The art activities will be choice-based and include 3D modular origami, zentangle drawings, magnetic stem art, and paper mosaics.
The class will walk through the 5-step modular origami triangle base fold, together and link together 3 of the triangles, at that point, the origami may be continued with simple patterns provided, or another project(s) may be chosen. The project time is flexible and an opportunity to try something new, or work on any preferred artwork.

item.title: 3D Sculpture Reliefs from Found Objects with Lisa MacNamara
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded: Learn how to create a sculptural form influenced by Louise Nevelson ( 1899-1988) Nevelson is known for her monochromatic wood assemblages, find treasures on the street, at the beach, in the garbage and yes, even in your closets! What kind of sculpture can you create from your treasures? This style of sculpting is a great narrative piece of your family, children, career etc., it’s your story to tell in a 3D genre. Techniques will include nailing, stapling, wire wrapping, threading, chemical bonding, liquid nails, cold connections and painting. The box for the wall relief is the most important unit to organize all your pieces. This workshop is designed to start and finish a sculpture, depending on intricacies

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: A wood or metal box with smaller boxes fitting into the larger one, various found objects representing your story for a wall relief. One quart or can of spray paint of your favorite color to paint entire sculpture. Recommend, interior flat house paint. Please note – water-based paints are best for this class

item.title: Memoir and Journal Writing with Rafael Lima
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded:
It should be easy to write a memoir or novel - the raw material – the experience of a lifetime - is familiar to us. Yet we must overcome the anxiety; will anyone consider our work worth reading?
If you have lived, you have a story to tell. Whether your life has been a thrill ride or relatively normal, there’s bound to be something fascinating about it; something uniquely yours.
In this workshop, you will learn the techniques of focusing your life stories into compelling narratives. Whether you seek to write a full-length memoir or even short journal entries we’ll show you how to best tell the stories from your life and how to get them published in the new world of digital self-publishing.
The workshop will be helpful for beginning writers as for those seasoned writers who want to be inspired in a supportive group setting – whether your goal is to finish that memoir or start a simple journal.

item.title: Drawing with Colored Pencil with Allison Berkner
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: The objective of this course would be to learn the basics of colored pencils, different types of paper, color theory, and drawing skills. · Ideally, the students will create 3 or 4 total drawings in colored pencil. · The technique would be for the instructor to have the class do color theory and colored pencil exercises leading up to their final pieces. · Starting with learning the color wheel, and diving into properties of color theory, the students will gain knowledge about how color interacts with itself and how it is perceived. · Going hand in hand, the students will also learn how to use colored pencils via different application techniques, shading and blending colors, as well as how paper can affect your drawing. · They will draw from photos as well as real life with objects. · Specific requirements for this course is to have a 12 pack of Prisma Colored Pencils, graphite pencils, multi-colored paper to help learn color theory, and other materials listed. · The course structure would be broken up within about every 2 classes. One class we will learn the basics of one thing, the next class we put that lesson into practice with a drawing; ex: one class we will learn and do exercises about cool tones/colors, the next class we will focus on a drawing that utilize those principles. Drawing with Colored Pencil Supply List

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Basic drawing, colored pencil, and color theory knowledge/background helpful but not required. This is a beginning/intermediate class.

item.title: Improvisational Quilting with Camille Perrin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This class will demonstrate the magic of working without a pattern and letting your “stash” speak for itself. We will work with shapes and fabric arrangements that do not follow any templates or rules. The outcome will be surprisingly beautiful and will spark the imagination for additional techniques with embellishments and top stitching. Bindings and finishing techniques will be discussed as well. Create an art piece, eye-catching bag, or functional quilt. A sewing machine in good working condition is necessary for this class. If you are a beginner or intermediate sewing artist, this class is for you.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Sewing machine straight stitch or 1/4" foot if available ● Assortment of quilting cottons ● 100% cotton thread ● Scissors ● pins ● 45mm rotary cutter - LAC has a few if you do not own

item.title: Introduction to Stained Glass Mosaic Workshop with Jennifer Rubinstein
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Learn everything you need to know to make a mosaic. We will cover substrates, materials, adhesives, and grouting. You will learn how to cut and shape glass using a scoring wheel and nippers. At the end of the second day, you will leave with a finished mosaic. Materials are included with additional materials available for purchase.
Please wear closed toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.
Email Carolyn@lighthousearts.org with any questions.

item.title: Feeling Relief-ed, Casting Glass Bas-relief Workshop with Jose Ugas
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Like Donatello’s rondelles, relief sculpting allows artist to create imagery and landscapes that rise from the background they are formed from. Using sculpting techniques to carve and build either the details of a familiar face or a scene from a zoomed ocean floor. This process will allow you to create a base and scene and then see that object casted in glass.

item.title: Introduction to Glass Casting Workshop with Jose Ugas
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Mold making is a fantastic method for creating amazing glass sculptures in the round (3-D). Using the this technique, the class will dive into how these skills and processes can be used to develop glass objects through the process of wax sculpting and glass casting.

item.title: Drawing with Ralph Papa
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This workshop is designed for individuals of all skill levels, from beginners eager to explore their artistic side to seasoned artists looking to refine their techniques. Join us in a welcoming and inspiring environment where you will learn the fundamentals of drawing while embracing the power of expressive lines. Ralph Papa will guide you through engaging exercises and projects, helping you discover the unique language of lines and their ability to convey emotions, movement, and depth. Drawing Class Supply List

item.title: Independent Study in Painting and Drawing with Jim Rigg
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This independent study course is designed for aspiring artists seeking a personalized and self-directed exploration of their artistic journey. Participants will have the opportunity to delve deeply into their chosen medium, develop their unique style, and refine their technical skills under the guidance of an experienced mentor.

item.title: Modern Take on China Paint
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
This hands-on, 2 day workshop is a modern take on traditional china painting surfaces. Students will be introduced to the materials and techniques used in the process of china painting on ceramics. Through a variety of exploring applications on both glazed surfaces (both white and colors) and unglazed bisque students will gain experience and know how to achieve desired design and surface decorations on their very own ceramic masterpieces.
Students are highly encouraged to bring in personal previously glazed work to decorate. All materials will be provided.

item.title: Painting Interior Scenes and Cafes with Eli Cedrone
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this workshop, you’ll learn the key concepts of painting interior scenes. Eli will demonstrate and explain her methods and work one-on-one with each student. The focus will be on: · How light flows through a scene, illuminating forms and creating an evocative mood. · Achieving accurate drawing and correct values; two of the most crucial aspects of representational painting. · How to develop a well-balanced composition of light and shadow patterns (chiaroscuro) · How to quickly block in the motif or major elements of the scene. · Balancing warm incandescent light with cool natural light · And lastly how to achieve value contrast and add finishing touches to your painting. Painting Interior Scenes and Cafes Supply List

item.title: Contemplating Clouds or Capturing the Ephemeral Light with Carin Wagner
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Using oil paints to achieve highly realistic cloudscapes, which can then form an essential part of your landscapes or on its own- gorgeous cloudscape – minimalist beauty. Wagner will demonstrate and guide students through the process, from blending the colors softly into each other maintaining clean colors and translucency, to building the more sculptural cloud formations. Preferably students will have previous experience with oils or acrylics. This technique uses small quantities of oil, worked in successive layers, with drying time hastened by walnut alkyd painting medium. Wagner will paint the same painting as the class so that each step is demonstrated. More advanced students may wish to work on independent pieces with guidance as needed. Individual attention will be offered at each stage.
Notice: April 15th class has been rescheduled to April 19th from 9am-12pm

Spring: $364 (Starts March 18th, No Class on April15)

item.title: Handbuilding I with Amalia Mermingas
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Learn a variety of handbuilding construction techniques; pinch pots, coil, and slab construction. Create decorative pieces, functional pieces, representations, or abstract sculptures. Students will finish projects using a variety of glazing methods.

item.title: Enameling: Sgraffito Workshop with Michel McNabb
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Using the technique of sgraffito, students will be able to draw through liquid glass enamel on a spun copper metal bowl to make beautiful, fun, and interesting layered surfaces.  Everyone will learn how to apply liquid, opaque, and translucent enamels to their metal as well as how to fire in a kiln. Students are encouraged to bring a source of inspiration – a drawing, image, etc. that they would like to render onto their piece. No experience is necessary, and ALL materials are included in your tuition.

item.title: For The Love of Art with Stephanie Blaskiewicz
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
This course is carefully crafted to nurture your child's artistic expression, cultivate their imagination, and foster a love for the creative process.
Throughout the program, students will embark on an exciting journey of self-discovery, where they will learn various art techniques, experiment with different mediums, and develop their unique artistic voice. The curriculum combines structured lessons with open-ended projects, allowing students to explore their creativity while building essential artistic skills.

item.title: Procreate 101 with Allison Berkner
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Create your own digital masterpieces. This class will teach the basics of the app including layers, brushes, and color palette usage. This course requires the attendee to bring an iPad with the Procreate app downloaded and an Apple Pencil (preferred) or compatible stylus.
ProCreate 101 Supply List

item.title: Paper, Textures and Painting - Watercolor, Acrylics and Oil Welcome! with Lisa MacNamara
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Paper, texture and painting - ALL THREE! Incoporate various papers into your paintings, watercolor, acrylics or oils, adding depth, texture and path findings through the painting Learn techniques using various tools, experiment with a fork or Xacto blade, or organic materials! Seeing what’s outside the box to enhance your narrative of your piece of art. Paper,Textures And Painting Supply List

item.title: Drawing with Colored Pencil with Allison Berkner
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: The objective of this course would be to learn the basics of colored pencils, different types of paper, color theory, and drawing skills. · Ideally, the students will create 3 or 4 total drawings in colored pencil.  The technique would be for the instructor to have the class do color theory and colored pencil exercises leading up to their final pieces. · Starting with learning the color wheel, and diving into properties of color theory, the students will gain knowledge about how color interacts with itself and how it is perceived. · Going hand in hand, the students will also learn how to use colored pencils via different application techniques, shading and blending colors, as well as how paper can affect your drawing. · They will draw from photos as well as real life with objects. · Specific requirements for this course is to have a 12 pack of Prisma Colored Pencils, graphite pencils, multi-colored paper to help learn color theory, and other materials listed. · The course structure would be broken up within about every 2 classes. One class we will learn the basics of one thing, the next class we put that lesson into practice with a drawing; ex: one class we will learn and do exercises about cool tones/colors, the next class we will focus on a drawing that utilize those principles. Drawing with Colored Pencil Supply List

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Basic drawing, colored pencil, and color theory knowledge/background helpful but not required. This is a beginning/intermediate class.

Suggested Materials:
  • Paper: Canson Mi-Teintes Pastel Pads (Assorted multi colored pack 9”x12” or 12”x16”)
  • Strathmore 400 series Toned Grey Sketch Pad 11”x14”
  • Strathmore 400 Series Colored Pencil Pad 12”x9” or 11”x14”
  • Optional/Other suggestions:
    • Strathmore 400 Series Heavyweight Drawing Pad 8”x10” or bigger—If you want extra paper or to have more variety than listed
    • A sketchbook/notepad no smaller than 5”x7” (I recommend something spiral bound, and a sketchbook made for dry materials, not wet or mixed media. This will be used for light sketching, practicing, exercises, note taking etc. Recommended brands are Canson or Strathmore. If you want to be exact, look for 80-140lbs pressed paper)
  • Pencils: Prisma Color Premiere 24 colored pencil set. It should have a butterfly on the cover of the packaging.
  • Graphite Pencils (At most, a 6 piece set is recommended 2H-6B, but not required, we will be using graphite pencils for light sketching)
  • Other Tools: A pencil sharpener (a metal pencil sharpener is highly recommended)
  • 1 regular eraser
  • 1 kneaded eraser
  • 12-inch ruler (metal cork back is highly recommended)
Materials can be purchased on dickblick.com, Amazon, Michaels, or any other art store you may like to go to! Dickblick and Amazon will most likely be the cheapest for supplies, but Michaels will sometimes have good deals/discounts!

item.title: Junk to 3D Story 2-Day Workshop with Lisa MacNamara
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Learn how to create a sculptural form influenced by Louise Nevelson (1899-1988) Nevelson is known for her monochromatic wood assemblages, find treasures on the street, at the beach, in the garbage and yes, even in your closets! What kind of sculpture can you create from your treasures? Include books, old art paintings, greeting cards, think outside the box! This style of sculpting is a great narrative piece of your family, children, career etc., it’s your story to tell in a 3D genre. Techniques will include nailing, stapling, wire wrapping, threading, chemical bonding, liquid nails, cold connections and painting. This workshop is designed to start and finish a sculpture.  Junk To 3D Story Supply List

item.title: Geometric Glass Patterns with Stringers with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Create a geometric look in fused glass with glass stringers. Intricate glass cutting skills .... a lot of it.....will be taught in this 4 week class. Students will create a sheet of glass using a specific layout of stringers. Once fused the glass will be cut up into pieces and cold worked then arranged in specific positions to create geometric patterns in your glass project. This technique is sure to be something you will utilize in your next fused glass project! Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase. Please wear closed toes shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.
Please email Carolyn with any questions at: Carolyn@lighthousearts.org

item.title: Modeling Glass Creations with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
By using a two-part Modeling Glass Mixture and a variety of bullseye glass powder colors you can turn them into a moldable, sculptable material similar to clay. The Powdered Binder is a food-grade, nontoxic cellulose-based material that reacts with water as a thickener. The Liquid Medium is also food-grade and nontoxic, and combines with water to give body and smoothness to the Modeling Glass, while preventing stickiness. Both the Binder and the Liquid Medium burn away during firing, leaving pure glass behind. Students will learn how to mix various colors of powders, how to blend and the use of a variety of tools to sculpt and mold their modeling glass into a one of a kind sculpture that can be free standing, displayed in a frame, or on an easel. Discussions on how certain colors and textures are achieved and mature using certain firing temperatures along with group discussion on the endless possibilities of this glass medium. This technique may then be used on larger fused glass works once you become familiar with the process in our upcoming Independent Study classes or Open Studio.
Please email Carolyn with any questions at: Carolyn@lighthousearts.org.
Materials and firing schedules are included with additional materials and firings schedules available for purchase. Please wear closed toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron. N95 mask will be provided when working with powders.

item.title: Garden Party with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Create unique fused glass objects to decorate your garden or patio with. In this 4 week class you will learn intricate cutting, fusing and slumping techniques and how to use cold working tools to design and create flowers, butterflies and other objects in a variety of colored glass. Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase.  Please wear closed toes shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron. Please email Carolyn with any questions at: Carolyn@lighthousearts.org

item.title: Earrings with Lisa Johnson
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
During this workshop, you'll learn how to make beautiful, stylish earrings! Students will learn how to solder a sterling silver post and make a French ear wire in addition to various texturing techniques to non-ferrous metals including silver. All materials are included! No experience is necessary.
Registration deadline June 5

item.title: Torch Fired Enamels with Lisa Johnson
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Learn how to make a colorful pendant and pair of earrings using fused glass on metal! Patterns will be developed through sifting, stenciling, and graphite techniques. In this workshop, we will build enameled surfaces on nonferrous metal to make a beautiful jewelry pieces. No experience necessary!

item.title: Kiln Carved Glass with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Make a lasting impression in glass using kiln carving techniques to create a beautiful kiln carved serving dish. Students will learn how to cut and work with fiber papers to create designs that will then be "carved out" into an 8 x 8 piece of glass. Learn to prepare your mold for slumping and how glass is formed in the kiln. Please wear closed toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron. Mask will be provided when working with fiber papers. Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase.

item.title: Fused Glass Basics with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Bring your creative ideas to this 3 hour workshop and learn the many possibilities of using a variety of colored glass, stringers and frit to create a one of a kind functional 8 x 8 piece of art glass that you will be proud to use and display. Students will learn how to properly use the tools and materials required to assemble and lay out a design on glass along with the firing schedules to fuse and slump your glass project. Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase.
Please wear closed toes shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.

item.title: Rings and Earrings Teen Workshop with Taylor Gigante
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this 1-day workshop, teens will learn to develop jewelry using traditional fabrication methods. Demonstrations include how to size and form a sterling silver ring as well as for earrings. Shaping the metal with a mallet, creating texture, and wire working will be introduced to students in order to complete a ring and earrings. Teens enrolled in this course must be responsible and comfortable using a tools such as hammers and handling a lit acetylene torch under supervision.

item.title: Found Object Art Collage Teen Workshop
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Recycle and reimagine old discarded junk into a one of a kind piece of art. Using found objects, old jewelry, odd bits of paper, fabric, feathers, and things you might find in a kitchen junk drawer, you will create a layered college or fantasy mask. No experience necessary, Just bring your imagination.

item.title: Sun Catchers and Coasters with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen

item.title: Paper Mache Sculpture with Lisa MacNamara
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this class, you'll dive into the exciting world of sculptural paper creation, with a little bit of paper, glue and paint. Whether you envision crafting a fantasy figure, an intriguing animal, or a unique concept entirely your own, the possibilities are limitless. Through the manipulation of wire, paper materials, and found objects, you'll have the chance to shape your vision into reality.

item.title: Glass Screen Printing with Penny Burdick
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
The objective of this fun class is to learn the process of screen-printing on glass mixed enamels. This will be a 2-day class in creating a beautiful plate using paints, silkscreens & EZ Fire Enamels. Students will paint the background on a white piece of glass with paints & sponges. Those plates will be fired, and the 2nd day students paint a silk screen they purchased from AAE Glass with white or Black EZ Fire Enamels. After the image is printed, clear glass will be put under the plates & it will be fused to make a small, slumped plate or decorative wall piece All materials are included except silk screens.
<u>The studio will provide a couple of different silk screens to use. If </u><u>s</u><u>tudents are interested in purchasing their own, they will need to order “simple screens” by May 27<sup>th</sup> from </u><u>AAE glass.com.</u>

item.title: Paint Your Favorite Animal with Robyn Price
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Create a one-of-a-kind portrait of your favorite animal using acrylic paint with an abstract, pop-art technique. Each painting will focus on using a color palette of your choice to establish the dark and light values of the reference image. This style focuses more on how different colors may be used to represent shadow and light in order to create a graphic-like painting. No blending or formal painting training should be required. It would be advisable to bring in your reference image in both color and black and white (or have such images readily available on your phone) and may be useful to research different color palette schemes that you may be interested in using. Please send in the image you would wish to paint a few days before the class to allow time the canvas to be prepped with a basic outline sketch—this course will focus more on the painting technique than drawing the image itself. All supplies are included.

item.title: Designing a Studio Painting from Photo or Plein Air Painting with Mary Garrish
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Mary Garrish will explain the 6 principles of design – line, shape, value, color, edges and texture. She will show you how she uses these to take a plein air painting or photo to design a larger studio painting. There will be multiple demos explaining these six principles and how to implement them. The course is designed to take you from thumbnail sketches to value studies and on to a finished painting.

item.title: Not Your Mother's Embroidery Sampler! with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Join the slow-stitching movement! Or, refresh your memory of an old, favorite hobby with this non-traditional embroidery workshop.
Learn fresh, or brush up, on sewing basics in a zero-judgment zone! Go home with a hand-sewn sample of stitchery that doubles as a ready-to-hang piece of art.
With group demos and one-on-one help, students will work at their level with different beads, fabrics, flosses, hoops, needles, notions, and even disappearing ink! Embroidery stitches, bead-work, and other embellishment techniques will be taught to create small, quick, and easy pieces for the home, or to give as a gift. Designs rotate seasonally and are always changing!

item.title: Figurative Sculpture: The Portrait
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This class provides an in-depth look at creating compelling figurative sculptures focusing on the portrait bust.  Reference photos are the responsibility of each student. The instructor will offer an approach to portraiture that focuses on anatomical structure, mapping, proportion, and capturing the individuality of each subject. Students will develop concepts through the incorporation of facial expressions, gestures, and thematic imagery.

item.title: Wet Carving Concrete with Elder Jones
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this 3-day workshop, each person will make a 20-30lb sculpture or planter. Day 1 - We dry mix sand and cement together and set it aside in 5 gallon buckets. We prepare our forms and turntable workstations then have a computer slide show presentation of the technique and my work. Day 2 - 9AM – 6PM. We start immediately upon arrival where we mix water into our dry mix and get it into the forms. We wait until it is set and, usually right after lunch, we carve our soft, setting (slowly getting harder) matrix until we are finished. Day 3 - Now that our work has set overnight it has cured enough to move. We remove it from our workstations, trim the foot, hose it off and clean up the area. View Elder Jones's work at SandPudding.com

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Optional: dust masks (I have these available as well. Some are used) Some people like to use disposable rubber gloves. I offer a set of 10 carving tools for sale, $25 for those that may want them. Otherwise I provide enough carving tools for the entire class to share. No materials fee.

item.title: Sculpting the Self: Portraiture in Clay with Jamie Bates
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: During this workshop students will learn to look at the human figure objectively by breaking it down into its’ parts. Students will begin by sculpting the eyes, nose, mouth, and ears creating multiple tiles and small vignettes. This exercise will lead to creating complete a portrait out of clay. Each piece will be built solid and hollowed out for complete freedom while sculpting. The self-portraits will begin with general rules of proportion and will end with a complete detailed image of the sculptor. Anatomy, underlying bone structure, musculature, expression, clay and surface will be discussed. Underglaze decorating techniques will be discussed if time permits. This workshop is open to all skill levels.

item.title: Setting it UP! with Lisa Johnson
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this class, we will review a few ways to include your unique gem into a ring, pendant, bracelet, and/or earrings. Demonstrations will cover tension setting a faceted stone, settings with a tooled edge, and back setting for a thick edge. We will develop interesting designs around your special stone to give it a contemporary look. Students must have experience with a jeweler’s saw and torch.

item.title: Fiber Art Jewelry with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
"Bring love letters, old clothing, jewelry scraps, paper momentos, and an open mind to this innovative fiber art jewelry workshop. Learn simple ways to preserve and transform paper and fabric momentos by combining them with traditional jewelry components to make a pair of earrings, or a pendant. Earrings can be of indefinite length (hello my concert junkies and statement earring peeps!) or as small as everyday posts, for an understated look.
Preserve bits of books, greeting cards, failed paintings, handwriting, love letters, old papers, precious concert tees, special occasion dresses, ticket stubs, and more in this unique workshop. Using just a few stitches (literally), some dye, a handful of fabric scraps, a bead or two, and a little acrylic, students will create their own jewelry pieces with deep sentimental value, or make fun statement pieces that are both large and lightweight.
All tastes can be accommodated. This beginner-friendly workshop will approach the basics of the fiber arts in a fun and accessible way.

item.title: Cottagecore Denim: Embellishing Jeans with Embroidery & More with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Bring jeans, dish towels, button down shirts, denim jackets, and miniskirts to this fun and fashionable fiber art workshop. Learn simple ways to embellish your wardrobe by adding beaded and embroidered accents to your clothing! Make one of a kind threads that express your unique personality. Learn embroidery stitches and hand sewing skills, laugh, and relax in this fun and creative workshop for free-spirited clothes horses. All tastes can be accommodated. This beginner-friendly workshop will approach the basics of the fiber arts, including using hand-sewing tools and techniques, in a fun and accessible way. Please bring a personal fabric item (non-stretchy) to embellish with embroidery and beads. And get ready to rock.

item.title: Wearable Art: Silkscreens & Block Printing with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Create functional, wearable, hand-printed art! In this beginner-friendly fiber art class, students will be introduced to silkscreen and linoleum block printing on fabric. Through group demos, one-on-one guidance, and hands-on experience, students will learn about printing techniques, tools, fabrics, and inks. Each student will learn to make and print a 2-3 color design. Students will work with silkscreen supplies, such as drawing fluid & screen filler, as well as block printing supplies, like barens and brayers, to create a design, transfer it to a block and/or screen, and print it with ink onto a functional or wearable piece of fabric.
Projects rotate seasonally and include items like aprons, tote bags, t-shirts, and more. Class permitting, hand-dyeing techniques will be taught. No prior experience required! All materials are included.

item.title: Making Beautiful Jewelry with Tracey Roedl
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Jewelry lovers- are you ready to get creative in a warm, inspiring group atmosphere? Tracey will guide you through using silver, gold, or other nonferrous metals (copper, brass, etc..) to make a twisted rings, pair of earrings, and pendant. Learn about design, soldering and forming metal, setting stones, and surface finishing techniques to make beautiful jewelry. Materials on the first day are covered by the Lighthouse ArtCenter. Please see the student material list for additional supplies. This list will also be reviewed during the first day in case there are questions.

item.title: Orbits Collar with Maracole Bijoux
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Join this fun, colorful jewelry making workshop to learn how to hand-weave Maracole’s colorful Orbits Necklace! During this workshop, you will master a simple beading stitch called Herringbone Stitch. In this case, you will have to implement both the flat and the tubular stitch to include a clasp as well as capture fun, spherical accents. Maracole will bring materials with her, but not all supplies. Please see the small student material list for this workshop.

item.title: Mini Textile Art Collage with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Look like a domestic goddess and learn how to create easy, hand-sewn collages!
These simple, colorful designs can be mounted to a greeting card and sent as happy mail. They can be matted and framed, or hung on the wall, as-is. This beginner-friendly workshop will approach the basics of fiber art and sewing in a fun (promise) and accessible way.
Using just a few stitches (literally), a handful of fabric scraps, and some stickerbacked fabric that disappears in water, students will create textile collages of florals, animals, landscapes, and other simple shapes. Matted collages can be framed, hung on walls, or given as gifts.
Designs will rotate seasonally and can be adapted to meet the needs of every student. All levels of expertise are welcome. Materials are inlcuded!

item.title: Mini Textile Art Collage with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Look like a domestic goddess and learn how to create easy, hand-sewn collages!
These simple, colorful designs can be mounted to a greeting card and sent as happy mail. They can be matted and framed, or hung on the wall, as-is. This beginner-friendly workshop will approach the basics of fiber art and sewing in a fun (promise) and accessible way.
Using just a few stitches (literally), a handful of fabric scraps, and some stickerbacked fabric that disappears in water, students will create textile collages of florals, animals, landscapes, and other simple shapes. Matted collages can be framed, hung on walls, or given as gifts.
Designs will rotate seasonally and can be adapted to meet the needs of every student. All levels of expertise are welcome. Materials are inlcuded!

item.title: Crochet Mini Christmas Stockings with Jennifer Noelle
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this crochet workshop, we will be learning how to crochet mini christmas stockings! It is recommended to have a basic understanding of crochet, but it's not essential to complete this fun project. We will be working with double crochets and learning how to front post, and back post double crochet. These mini stockings are great to make for gifts or to add a festive touch to your holiday decor. Materials are inlcuded!

item.title: Coffee Mug Cozy Crochet Pattern with Jennifer Noelle
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this beginner friendly crochet workshop, students will learn how to crochet a coffee mug cozy. This cozy is worked in the tradiaitional granny stitch which makes it a great project for both beginner & intermediate crocheters. Durig the workshop, the instructor will guide you through each phase of the crochet process with writen, verbal, and hands-on instruction that allows you to complete your project with ease. Materials are included!

item.title: Sea Turtle Crochet Coaster with Jennifer Noelle
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this beginner friendly crochet workshop, students will learn how to crochet a super cute sea turtle coaster. Perfect for beginners, this vlass will teach you essential crochet techniques like chain stitches, single crochet, and double crochet. Create a functional and decorative piece that adds a touch of ocean- inspired style to your home.

item.title: Advanced Oil Painting with Manon Sander
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
This is a class for the artist who is comfortable with their medium and is ready to take their work to a new level: Ignite your thinking about design, graduate from copying your subject matter to creatively exploring it, learn how to assess your own work in order to make informed decisions about necessary improvements, learn about different materials and mediums, express yourself more freely through expressive brush work and mark making. Demos and lectures will be on an as-needed basis, the rest of the class will be individual instruction. You will work from your own reference material.
Fall: Members Only: $272 Class Dates: 11/6, 11/13, 11/20, 12/4, 12/11

*Please call the gallery to register: 561-746-3101

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
Bring what you have.
No smelly turpenoids please: Gamsol only for oil painters

item.title: Exploring Abstraction with Stella Vasilopoulos
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Explore the principles and techniques of abstract art. In these classes, individuals are encouraged to express themselves freely through paint, color, and form, without necessarily adhering to representational or realistic styles. Participants often experiment with various materials, techniques, and styles to develop their own unique artistic voice.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• One medium to large sized canvas
  • One small canvas or piece of foam board
  • A small, medium, and large paint brush
  • A minimum of three analogous colors"

item.title: Painting with Acrylics with Caroline Duran
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This course is an introduction to the basics of acrylic painting. Students will learn about creating a successful composition, methods of transfering a contour outline, mixing observed values and colors based on selected reference photo, application of paint to canvas, and brushstroke techniques. The instructor will assist each student in the planning and painting process from start to finish. This course is entry level, accessible for all, and individualized to meet each student’s skill level. No prior art experience is required. Each student should bring a laptop or Ipad to each class to view their reference photo while painting.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• Laptop/tablet required every class to view references while painting
  • Canvas as needed based on pace- 8 x 10 in minimum and 11 x 14 in. maximum size suggested
  • Acrylic Paint Brushes- soft flat, round, and detail brushes of various sizes
  • Acrylic Paint- Liquitex suggested
    • (Colors- red, blue, yellow, white, black, raw umber or dark brown)
  • Palette
  • 3-5 photos of possible subjects ranging from animals, landscapes, still life objects, flowers, etc. Photos must be clear on zoom, true to color, and well-lit. Simplified subjects suggested for beginners.

item.title: Painting a Sunlit Cottage with Kathleen Denis
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Learn how to capture a charming, sunlit cottage that Kathleen is so well known for! She will teach you step-by-step all the elements that make a captivating painting, filled with light. In addition to learning what colors to use to exaggerate the light, she will include what to look for in compositional elements, focal point and color harmony, including how to capture a good photograph to use for a painting. Weather permitting, we will go outside to observe the sunlight and shadow. Kathleen will provide photographs for you to paint from or you may bring your own. Kathleen is an award-winning artist and a generous, thorough teacher who also spends individual time with each student. Her paintings and accreditations may be viewed at www.KathleenDenis.com.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Any level is acceptable, but a working knowledge of your medium is necessary, as Kathleen will not be teaching how to use a medium.

item.title: Optic Glass Cover Up
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Cover Up is a sequel to our Optic classes, where we use glass stringers and Capz , stacks of glass, to create a unique, optical look in fused glass. In this 4 week class you will learn the basics of working with stringers and the art of cutting, grouping and laying out a specific pattern to complete a one of a kind functional art glass project. We will use some of the same techniques in our last class but changing the parameters and glass color to make a very different piece along with 2 small companion pieces. Some cutting skills recommended. Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase.
Please wear close-toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.
Please Email Carolyn with any questions at: Carolyn@LighthouseArts.org

item.title: Fused Glass Gingerbread Houses with Jennifer Rubinstein
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Create a stunning, almost edible looking gingerbread house from glass.
In this one day workshop you will learn everything you need to know to create a colorful, scrumptious and festive gingerbread house. Students will learn how to draw and lay out your plans for the construction of a glass house using the basic glass fusion techniques for cutting glass along with a wide variety of accessory glass, glass line paints and more to decorate and accessorize your gingerbread house.
Materials and firing schedules are included with additional materials and firings available for purchase. Please wear closed toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.
Please email Carolyn with any questions at: Carolyn@lighthousearts.org

item.title: Glass, Mixed Media and Found Objects Mosaics with Jennifer Rubinstein
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Mix it up! In this class we will be using all kinds of tesserae-glass, ceramic pieces, found objects, beads, and costume jewelry to make a truly, unique statement piece mosaic! We will discuss non traditional substrates and will be using Apoxie Sculpt as the adhesive to achieve a truly textural art piece. If you have nostalgic pieces of costume jewelry please bring them. No experience is necessary.
Materials and firing schedules are included with additional materials and firings schedules available for purchase. Please wear closed toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.
Please email Carolyn with any questions at: Carolyn@lighthousearts.org

item.title: Intro to Glass Fusing with Jennifer Rubinstein
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Learn the fundamentals of kiln formed glass to create a one of a kind project from beginning to end. Students will be introduced to the many tools, materials and supplies that are used in the basic method of glass fusion. From design layout and preparation of your glass, cutting techniques, and firing schedules to the cold work and slumping needed to complete your project. A great lesson to work through the process of making a beautiful kiln formed piece of glass art. You will walk away with the knowledge to move on to more advanced classes.
Materials and firing schedules supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase. Closed toed shoes required
Email Carolyn@lighthousearts with any questions.

item.title: Intro to Glass on Glass Mosaic with Jennifer Rubinstein
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Learn everything you need to make a glass on glass (GOG) mosaic.
Using clear glass as the base, and transparent glass as the “tesserae," you will create a translucent mosaic that allows the light to shine through.
During the first session you will learn the technical skills to cut and shape the glass as well as design and flow ideas. The second day will be devoted to grouting and finishing your mosaic.
Bring your idea sketched or drawn on an 8X10" piece of paper or will have drawings ready for you.
Materials included.
Please email Carolyn with any questions at :Carolyn@lighthousearts.org

item.title: Book Club: The "Art" of Reading with Ruth Mamo
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
In this class, you'll read a novel and share your thoughts and ideas through writing and art. You'll use mediums such as painting, collage, or mixed-media to create an art journal based on the story. The teacher will guide you with writing prompts and group discussions to help you reflect on the book and express your personal connections creatively.
This class is perfect for anyone who loves both art and storytelling and wants to explore how they connect. For the winter session, we’ll be reading The Bird Hotel by Joyce Maynard.
Please read Chapters 1-10 before the first class!

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: The “Art” of Reading: Supply List and Syllabus Book: The Bird Hotel by Joyce Maynard Bare Books (I have mixed media books for your use on this project) both landscape and/or portfolio.) If you’d like your own personal mixed media journal, please feel free to bring your own. You can decided either way once class begins. Canvas/Watercolor paper Watercolors Acrylics Pastels Ink Gauche Brushes Pencils Erasers Collage Items Lined writing paper Week One: January 9th, 2025 Before attending the first class, please read Chapters 1-10 of the Bird Hotel by Joyce Maynard 1pm-1:30pm Literary Luminosity: Round Table Book Discussion 1:30-2:00 Reflective Writing Prompt: Paint Me Like I Am 2:30-4:00 Creative Reflection through visual art drawing, painting, collage, etc. Week Two: January 16th: Chapters 11-25 1pm-1:30pm Literary Luminosity: Round Table Book Discussion 1:30-2:30 Reflective Writing Prompt: Thirteen Ways of Looking at a Blackbird 2:30-4:00 Creative reflection through visual art drawing, painting, collage, etc. Week Three: January 23rd: Chapters 26-46 1pm-1:30pm Literary Luminosity: Round Table Book Discussion 1:30-2:30 Reflective Writing Prompt: How to Be… 2:30-4:00 Creative reflection through visual art drawing, painting, collage, etc. Week Four: January 30th: Chapters 47-60 1pm-1:30pm Literary Luminosity: Round Table Book Discussion 1:30-2:30 Reflective Writing Prompt: Letter to… 2:30-4:00 Creative reflection through visual art drawing, painting, collage, etc. Week Five: February 6th: Chapters 61-78 Week Six: February 13th: Chapters 79-91 Week Seven: February 20th: Chapters 92-100 (End of Book) Week Eight: February 28th: Final showcase and sharing of Journals *I hope this helps…weeks five through seven will be conducted in the same manner as weeks one through four.

item.title: Let it Flow Pattern Bars with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Let the glass flow in this fun 4 week class! Create a one of a kind fused glass platter or free standing art piece for decorative and / or functional use.Students will learn how heat, viscosity and gravity work to create unique organic designs in glass.Mix and match a variety of glass colors to create bars of beautiful glass layers that will be tack fused together. The glass bars will be fused into individual stacks so there is no need to use a tile saw after the fusing. The glass will then be set up in unique patterns in a prepared mold that will controll the flow and form in the final fusing. Coldworking the glass using diamond hand lap pads and grinders will be taught to finish off the edges. A variety of slumping molds will be available to create the final shape of the one of a kind piece of art glass you will be proud to use and display! Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase. Please wear closed toes shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.
Please email Carolyn with any questions at :Carolyn@lighthousearts.org

item.title: Mixed Media with Danuta Rothschild
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this workshop, you will learn different textures, collage , composition, values and how to mix colors. You will be creating Portraits, landscapes, abstracts and three dimensional pieces using the above elements.

item.title: Saddle-set Hinged Earrings with Alex Boyd
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This class is all about teensy tiny moving parts. They can seem intimidating at first but with a little guidance you’ll be crushing it. And by crushing it I actually mean not crushing it because then they wouldn’t work anymore. I’ll cover building 22k gold bezels for cabochons, making saddle settings for drilled stones, making tiny hinges and riveting them together without freezing the hinge, making a little swivel hook for ear wires so that the earrings don’t go flying off the next time you’re headbanging in the mosh pit, and tons of other little tips and tricks that have applications in all sorts of scenarios.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
Materials Kit: $160 – paid directly to instructor, Alex Boyd.  Includes the following below: 
  • 2 matching cabs 
  • 2 drilled paddle-shaped stones 
  • .925 sheet 16 gauge approximate 2cm x 2cm (large enough to back 2 bezels) 
  • .925 22 gauge 3.4mm x 4.5cm 
  • .925 22 gauge 2.3mm x 5cm 
  • .925 22 gauge 1.6mm x 3cm 
  • .925 tubing 1.7mm outer diameter .9mm inner diameter 9mm long 
  • .925 round wire 20 gauge 10cm 
  • Bezel wire 22k gold or fine silver 24 gauge tall enough and long enough to set cabs 18k 
  • or .925 20 gauge round wire 3.5cm 
  • Hard silver solder 
  • 18k yellow hard solder (if using gold) 
  Files:  Note: The tools mentioned below are those that I’ll be using in my demonstrations. Often there are multiple tools that can achieve the same result. I use high quality tools, but you can usually get by with the economy versions (except for files, good files make all the difference). If you have any questions, please email me at alex@alexboydstudio.com.  #2 cut needle file set #4 cut needle file set  #2 and #5 cut flat hand files  Note about files: Exact needle files used will vary depending on the shape of the cabochons chosen. This project can be made with a basic economy needle file set and a #2 cut flat hand file but it will be more difficult to achieve a high degree of craftsmanship.  Pliers:  Chain nose pliers Round/flat pliers Parallel pliers Half round pliers Flat nose pliers Flush cutters    Scribe  Planishing hammer ( LAC has a couple in the studio if you don’t have one)  Sanding sticks in 180, 320 and 600 grit (Make your own from loose paper and a paint stirring stick)  Iron wire birds nest (make your own with black annealed steel wire. Never use galvanized) Free tutorial available at www.alexboydstudio.com. (LAC has wire in the studio)  Jeweler’s saw (LAC has in the Studio)  2/0 and 6/0 saw blades  .7mm drill bit 1mm krauss bur  1.4mm ball bur Flexshaft or micromotor Burlife or beeswax Toothbrush  Third hand tweezers   Dividers  Medium grit 3M bristle disc   Pin vise  Fine point permanent marker   Bezel roller
