item.title: Portrait: Sculpting the Human Head with Eduardo Gomez Rojas
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This Workshop will cover anatomical proportions and basic anatomy of the head to complete the human head and neck and a nuanced portrait of a live model. We will use the planes of the face to obtain a general likeness and then move forward with different ways of modeling the nose, lips, ears and eyes using specific modelling tools. Anatomical rendering issues will be studied related to aging, race, and facial expressions. Certain surface finishing and mounting techniques will also be covered. This class includes 25lbs of low fire clay, firing, and live model.

item.title: Full Figure: Sculpting the Human Body with Eduardo Gomez Rojas
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Students will cover basic anatomy of the head, body and anatomical proportions by observing a live model. We will cover issues related to design and mounting of the sculpture. We will also study different ways of modeling the individual parts such as the hands and feet nose, lips, ears and eyes. Certain surface finishing techniques will also be covered. The class will cover how to hollow the sculpture to get it ready for firing. 25 lbs of clay included and one firing.

item.title: The Diminutive Teapot and Dwippy Glaze Play with Fong Choo
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
In this 2-Day 3-Wings Workshop, students will watch Choo create his master pieces using the potter’s wheel and other hand building techniques. He will explore his utilitarian roots: creating and exploring bowls, mugs, vases and platters. Choo will give the secrets behind his “Dwippy” methods of glaze play. This somewhat unorthodox method demonstrates and is designed to create a dazzling palette of finishes. Results have been described many ways: Luscious. Random. Runny. Marbly. Amazing. And ‘Dwippy.’ Choo likes to say “They’re so loose they slide.
Students have the opportunity to glaze 1or 2 of their very own bisqued pots in the “Dwippy” style after the Demo. Must be cone 6 or High fire clay (ex. B-Mix) and NO larger than 8 inches in any direction. (Highly Recommended) Choo is also highly regarded for his use of alternative materials in his handles. Attendees will be shown creative ways to use cane and reed in handle assemblages for the teapots.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• Notebook and pen/pencil,
  • 2-3 brushes,
  • 1-2 bisqueware pots/forms made with cone 6 or high fire clay.
  • No large than 8 inches.
  • Contact LAC, 3D Studio if you have questions about clay.

item.title: Casting a New Look on Things with Lisa Johnson
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Discover the process of creative lost wax casting to make one-of-a-kind jewelry! Utilizing this ancient technique, students will develop wearable, fun, expressive, rings and necklaces or pendants. Reductive and additive techniques in wax working, casting of found objects, investing, pouring metal, and some soldering fabrication techniques will be demonstrated during this workshop. Each student will design their own compositions as they select a few organic things (leaf, bug, branch, lace, etc..) to cast and transform into adornment giving it a new look that displays both recognizable and abstract elements. Participants in this course will leave knowing how to cast using non-ferrous metals into a creation of their own. This workshop is open to all levels. However, using a jeweler’s saw and familiarity with using a torch is helpful but not required.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: 2oz of sterling silver casting grain and/or sodler free sterling silver scrap metal (old rings, pendants,earrings)

item.title: Sip and Paint with Stephanie Blaskiewicz
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Unleash your creativity at our Sip and Paint class, where you'll create a stunning 8x8 piece using acrylic paint. Enjoy a relaxing evening with a glass of wine in hand as our instructor guides you step-by-step, making it easy for artists of all levels to bring their vision to life. Perfect for a fun night out or a creative escape!

item.title: Art for the Homeschooled with Stephanie Blaskiewicz
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Enroll your home-schooled child in our engaging art class, designed to explore a variety of artistic styles and mediums. From painting and drawing to mixed media, this class encourages creativity and self-expression while teaching fundamental art techniques. Perfect for nurturing young artists in a supportive and inspiring environment. All supplies included.

item.title: Adding Figures to your Paintings in a Natural Way with Michele Byrne
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Michele will show you how to add natural looking figures to your paintings using palette knife or bold brush strokes. She will also teach you how to compose your paintings using strong design, value, temperature and paint manipulation. Starting with a small Value Study/Thrust Map for the design and then moving onto the canvas. You will start your canvas with a strongly designed underpainting and then add the colors with the correct values and color chroma. Finishing with thick paint and then paint manipulation to create a powerful and dramatic impressionistic painting full of life and movement. Michele will do daily demonstrations in the mornings followed by student work time with lots of one-on-one help. On day one you will paint from live models to gain confidence in creating believable body language of your subjects. On day two you’ll design a strong piece from beginning to end. On day three you’ll continue with your painting or start a new one. Please bring your own photos or use some that I will supply. This will be an indoor class working from photos. It will be a fun and information packed workshop!

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
Supply List: For Value Studies (quick sketches of what you will paint)

I’ll be using an https://www.edgeprogear.com (Passport size) (THIS IS THE ONE I USE FOR TRAVEL) Or an Open Box M – comes in many sizes. Smaller is better for travel. https://www.openboxm.com/#/

item.title: Texture in Watercolor with Lisa MacNamara
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Discover the art of crafting distinctive textures in watercolor to elevate the visual impact of your paintings. You'll explore different techniques for creating texture, you'll develop one or several color field paintings adorned with fresh textures. All supplies are included.

item.title: Bringing Exciting Light into your Paintings with Mark Shasha
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: One of the most common mistakes painters make is to forget to bring exciting light into their paintings. Even when compositions and other aspects work well something is often missing in the presentation of light. Mark will show you how to fix this problem by applying many of his favorite techniques acquired over his 40 years as a full time artist and illustrator. This fun, two day workshop will focus on the power of values which shift from light to dark. Whether you are a beginner or professional Mark will bring you to the next level. Expect each day to begin with some general lessons and at least one demo followed by one on one instruction for the rest of the day. A group critique will be available for anyone who would like to participate late in the afternoon on the second day. Students are encouraged to bring any medium they feel comfortable with, Mark will be using oil paints.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
PAINTS:
  • Michael Harding oil paints are great. But bring any art supplies you feel most comfortable with.
  • Cadmium Yellow
  • Medium Lemon Yellow
  • Ultramarine Blue
  • Cadmium Orange
  • Permanent Green
  • Light Green
  • Earth (Terra Verte)
  • Cobalt Blue
  • Phthalocyanine (Phthalo) blue
  • Raw Umber
  • Cadmium Red
  • Light Alizarin
  • Crimson
  • Dioxazine Purple
  • Titanium White
  •  Avoid student grade paints or any cheap paints.
ART MATERIALS:
  • An outdoor painting easel or pochade box. I use the M Box pochade with a tripod. Strata or French half easels is fine. There are many brands.
  • Odorless Turpentine or Gamsol
  • a clear painting gel.
  • An assortment of large and small brushes.
  • Palette knife
  • Paper Towels
  • A value scale (shows white to black and the grays in between)
  • A small sketchpad. Grey toned is best.
  • One black charcoal pencil, One white charcoal pencil and a kneeded eraser for making thumbnail sketches.
  • A few canvas panels panels (9x12, 8x10, 11x14) already primed with either acrylic or oil-based gesso (Sourcetek, Raymar and Centurian are good) avoid Fedrix panels if possible. I don’t recommend stretched canvas for this workshop.
  • Viewfinder (I like “the Viewcatcher” but bring whatever you like)
OTHER IMPORTANT ITEMS:
  • A hat with a wide brim
  • Sunscreen
  • Bug spray
  • Small plastic bags for your trash
  • Sense of humor - outdoor painting can be physically and emotionally challenging.
OPTIONAL:
  • A lightweight folding chair – if you like to sit while you paint
  • A small folding tray which can open easily as a side table if you like that sort of thing (I do)
  • A Medium sized color shaper (it has rubber-tip on the end, looks like a large eraser)

item.title: Paint Cows! and Other Farm Animals with Stephen Wysocki
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
On the first day, We will visit a local farm with cows and other livestock where we will take studies and sketches, and hopefully finish a Plein Air painting.
Our second day will be used to paint from our sketches and Plein Air paintings that we did on the previous day to use to finish a studio painting.

  • A painting style umbrella
  • Garbage bag (trash collection)
  • Panels for our Plein Air Day smaller panels for our Plein Air studies …..example 6x8, 8x10 or 9x12.
  • Panels for our Studio day larger panels…example 11x14, 12x16 or 14x18.
  • My paint list …oil paints

  • Phthalo Green
  • Phthalo Blue
  • Cadmium Yellow Deep
  • Cadmium Orange
  • Cadmium Red Pale (a deeper orange)
  • Naphthol Red Medium
  • Titanium White

item.title: Let's Get Connected with Lisa Johnson
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Developing connections is what a lot of jewelry making is all about! In this workshop you will learn ways of forming and soldering chains and links using sterling silver to create a bracelet. We will finish it all off with a handmade clasp to fit your design. Demonstrations on fabrication skills such as soldering, forming, and surface finishes will be covered.

item.title: Mini Fiber Art Collage with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Look like a domestic goddess and learn how to create easy, hand-sewn collages!
These simple, colorful designs can be mounted to a greeting card and sent as happy mail. They can be matted and framed, or hung on the wall, as-is. This beginner-friendly workshop will approach the basics of fiber art and sewing in a fun (promise) and accessible way.
Using just a few stitches (literally), a handful of fabric scraps, and some stickerbacked fabric that disappears in water, students will create textile collages of florals, animals, landscapes, and other simple shapes. Matted collages can be framed, hung on walls, or given as gifts.
Designs will rotate seasonally and can be adapted to meet the needs of every student. All levels of expertise are welcome. Materials are included!

item.title: Resin Art with Aleshia Rae Wolanske
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Guided By Aleshia Rae Wolanske of A. Rae Of Sunshine Design.  Price Includes Everything.  Aleshia always encourages artistic freedom, and you will have many resin colors and embellishments to choose from.  Aleshia also focuses on personalizing art, adding intentions and making the process of creating of most importance.  You may also bring an item or items that are special to you and that you may want preserved in resin.  No experience needed.  She will teach you resin safety, design layout, how to prep your materials for resin, resin mixing & coloring, how to embed objects in resin, how to manipulate self-leveling resin with equipment, proper resin cleanup, proper resin curing and much more!  You will go home with your very own Resin Art creation!

item.title: Oil Painting with Calvin Liang
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
The workshop will consist of two days of outdoor painting and two days will be spent working on a single studio painting based on photos you take on location. Calvin will begin a slideshow to show how he uses the photo as reference for the painting, then do a demonstration and spend the remaining time with each student throughout the rest of the day. It is recommended to bring a laptop or tablet for the studio days. Alternatively, you may have color prints of your reference photos printed locally.
Plein air painting is a foundational part of training the eye to better understand the concepts of composition, design, and color harmony. The lessons will include:
  1. How to plan a composition that will be effective for the artist’s intentions and preferences
  2. How to better see and use warm and cool color in landscape
  3. How to command hardness and softness of the edges to create space in a painting
  4. How to simplify the subject matter through the use of basic design, value, color and drawing skills
  5. How to consider the reasons for different paint surface textures, and brushstroke direction over the forms
  6. How to get the best possible results in a short time.

  • Palette knife
  • Oil colors

item.title: Animal Portraits in Clay with Caroline Duran
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This class will explore the process of sculpting a realistic animal portrait by utilizing reference photos. Reference photos are the responsibility of each student, either a pet or perspective animal image. The instuctor will offer an approach to animal portraiture that focuses on anatomical structure, proportion, and capturing the individuality of each animal.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
Most tools needed can be purchased at 3D Studio ArtShop, Standard handbulding tools, brush for glazing, finishing sponges, and modeling/large loop tools, small Tupperware for slip, serrated/rubber ribs (red/blue), wire cutter, various paint brushes, sketchbook (optional), laptop to view reference photos while sculpting Highly Recommended:
  • Amazon.com: Xiem Tools Scraper Tool (Double-Ended) for Pottery and Ceramics

item.title: Carving a Whale Weathervane with Dennis Del Mauro
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Students will create a whale weathervane, not from copper or tin, but carved from wood. The student will finish his creation either in weathered paint or faux verdigris to simulate age. Both returning and new students will also have the option of carving a shorebird instead of the weathervane.

item.title: Acrylic Marbling On Papers & A Silk Scarf Too! with Peggy Wertheim
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This workshop will give you a taste of working with marbling patterns! Unlike many Art Forms which take years to master, marbling will inspire you with instant gratification and success! Traditional marbling techniques using carrageenan and acrylic paints will be demonstrated. You will learn various patterns to create marbled papers which you can then incorporate into greeting cards, collages, framed art, journal covers, etc. AND you will also create 1 MARBLED Silk Scarf. All materials and equipment are provided and included in your tuition.

item.title: Strip Cut Construction with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Create a one of a kind standing or functional piece of glass art in this 4 week class. Students will learn how to cut a number of glass strips out of various sheets of glass, some made with stringers and some factory made to place them on edge side-by-side in whatever patterns they desire.
They will then be fused together into a solid piece. Learn how the use of kiln furniture will be used to dam your project to form the solid piece of glass and then use various cold working methods to smooth the edges before slumping.
Materials and firing schedules are included with additional materials and firings schedules available for purchase.
Closed toed shoes required
Email Carolyn@lighthousearts.org with any questions

item.title: Setting it UP! with Lisa Johnson
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this class, we will review a few ways to include your unique gem into a ring, pendant, bracelet, and/or earrings. Demonstrations will cover tension setting a faceted stone, settings with a tooled edge, and back setting for a thick edge. We will develop interesting designs around your special stone to give it a contemporary look. Students must have experience with a jeweler’s saw and torch.

  • (2) 3mm round faceted stone – I have CZ’s that you can use! They were just donated. If you want a different color, you can purchase stones on riogrande or amazon.

item.title: Throwing and Altering: On the Potter's Wheel with Ray Brown
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Students will learn how to throw, alter and assemble pottery out of round. Objectives include being more comfortable altering forms, a further understanding of utility, and a iterative process of developing form. Emphasis will be given to asymmetry, stamping, and dynamic attachments. Students will learn how to alter at different stages, from wet to bone dry, as well as creating composition, and a unified surface. Students will be required to have a basic knowledge of throwing, as well as a willingness to alter out of the round.

item.title: Making a Relief from a Live Model with Eduardo Gomez Rojas
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Use your wonderfully skilled mark making techniques on clay and learn the secrets of combining your drawing and sculpting skills to make a relief sculpture. Each student will construct a clay rendering from a live model in the classroom. We will discuss the difference between a low, medium and high reliefs and the technical issues involved with each. Within the class structure we will also look at and discuss some famous relief artworks and how they used foreshortening/perspective successfully. No previous sculpture experience required, but some drawing proficiency is recommended. This workshop includes 25lbs of low fire clay and one firing.
** A separate finishing workshop (not included) will be held at a later date after first firing.**

item.title: Making your favorite Animal with Eduardo Gomez Rojas
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Working from an image, the student will develop a sculpture of their favorite animal. This can be accomplished as a 3D sculpture or as a relief sculpture depending on the animal pose and the final destination of the sculpture. Students will study the basic anatomy of the animal with reference anatomy books provided by the instructor. There will also be a discussion on sculpture design as well as finishing and mounting. No previous sculpture experience required. This workshop includes 25lbs of low fire clay and one firing.
** A separate finishing workshop (not included) will be held at a later date after firing.**

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• Basic Clay sculpting tools
  • Images of the pet or animal you are sculpting
  • Perfered print outs on 8.5 x 11 sheet of standard paper

item.title: Narrative Sculpture with Kelsey Bowen
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this course, students will work closely with figurative sculptor Kelsey Bowen to create clay figures that tell a story. Techniques covered in this workshop will include coil building, gesture, expression, and the use of objects to build a narrative within a 3-dimensional sculpture. The workshop will begin with the introductory techniques of sculpting the human figure in clay and move through the process of adding details to develop meaning. Kelsey will demonstrate the wet clay processes used to create her own work including anthropomorphic figurative sculpting, texturing, creating clothing with clay, and other detail-oriented sculpting techniques.

item.title: Glass Frit Inlays with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Taking glass frit to another level… Using crushed glass frit in your art projects can give you possibilities that are not available when working with sheet glass. You can arrange it into shapes that prove difficult to master when cutting glass. In this workshop we will fill vermiculite dams with stainless steel molds and contrasting colors of frit to create a geometric bowl using this inlaid frit technique. You can then have it slumped into a mold for a functional dish or hang it for display.
All materials and firing included. Additional materials and firings available for purchase.
Closed toed shoes Required.
Email Carolyn@lighthousearts.org with any questions

item.title: Fused Glass Animals Kids Art Re-imagined with Jennifer Rubinstein
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Remember making toilet paper roll and cardboard critters when you were young? We’re taking the idea one step further and making them in fused glass. In this 3 hour workshop you will create a cute animal while learning to use various glass cutting tools and a variety of colored glass and accesroies to choose create a one of a kind fun glass art piece your inner child will be sure to love!
Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase.
Please wear close-toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.
Email Carolyn Austin with any question at Carolyn@lighthousearts.org

item.title: Wire Wrapped Jewelry with Justin Alexander White
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Learn the fundamentals of wire wrapping while creating your own custom pieces of Jewelry in class. We will cover stone setting, wire weaving techniques, and framing techniques. Create your own pendant, earrings, or ring.
The objective of this class is to empower students at all levels to take their wrapping to the next level. After this session you will be confident in creating custom jewelry. Wire wrapping is a cold technique, meaning there is no heat or fusion of the metal. Stone settings are obtained purely through tension.
All you need is a bit of wire, some creativity and a smile.

• Jewelry plier set
  • Personal item to wrap
  • A small sketchbook
  • Wire of your choice
  • Metal Ring Mandrel (If student chooses to make rings

item.title: Fiber Art Jewelry with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
"Bring love letters, old clothing, jewelry scraps, paper momentos, and an open mind to this innovative fiber art jewelry workshop. Learn simple ways to preserve and transform paper and fabric momentos by combining them with traditional jewelry components to make a pair of earrings, or a pendant. Earrings can be of indefinite length (hello my concert junkies and statement earring peeps!) or as small as everyday posts, for an understated look.
Preserve bits of books, greeting cards, failed paintings, handwriting, love letters, old papers, precious concert tees, special occasion dresses, ticket stubs, and more in this unique workshop. Using just a few stitches (literally), some dye, a handful of fabric scraps, a bead or two, and a little acrylic, students will create their own jewelry pieces with deep sentimental value, or make fun statement pieces that are both large and lightweight.
All tastes can be accommodated. This beginner-friendly workshop will approach the basics of the fiber arts in a fun and accessible way.

item.title: Photography I with Dennis P. León
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This comprehensive photography class will take the students from the basics of camera use to an advanced level use of their digital cameras. The students will learn to abandon the Auto Mode to advance shooting modes, suitable for different situations. The students will learn the Exposure Triangle, Metering, Focusing Modes and more. This first part of the class will be complemented with weekly exercises. As the student comprehend the camera, then the students will explore and learn extensively, Composition, Color Theory, why shooting in Black and White, some portraiture, and more. One the first day students are asked to three printed photos that he or she would be proud to showcase, and a digital camera with a charged battery. Every week there will be exercises to reinforce the knowledge acquired, and practice Constructive Critique, by which the students learn how to “see” their photos and from other students, reinforcing the knowledge acquired.

item.title: Introduction to Digital Cameras Workshop with Dennis P. León
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: During this two day workshop, the students will become acquainted with their camera functions. The student will learn how to properly expose a photograph, learn about the Exposure Triangle, and how to translate to the final exposure with Exposure compensation, different Shooting Modes of the cameras, for total control. The student is required to bring a digital camera with a charged battery.

item.title: Composition for Digital Photographers with Dennis P. León
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This two day workshop is created for digital shooters, either digital cameras or smart phones. The students will understand the principles of composition to create memorable images. The image creator will understand the so called “rules of Composition” when to use them and when to break them, that will allow them to compose interesting images. The students also will learn about Color Theory, and its uses, why shooting in Black and White, Portraiture and more.

item.title: Introduction to Adobe’s Lightroom with Dennis P. León
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This four week class will introduce the student to the world of processing digital images using Adobe’s Lightroom. You will learn how to download, store and classify your images. Learn about the different modules available in Lightroom. We will spend most of the time in the Develop Module, performing Global Adjustments, Basic, Tone Curve, Color Mixer, etc., and Targeted Adjustments using Masks, Intersecting Masks, and more. Preparing the images for exporting to social media or Printing. This class is available for Digital Camera users and Smart Phone shooters as well.

item.title: Visible Mending with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Give beloved, well-worn belongings new life with this fun and creative hand sewing workshop! Learn different ways to visibly patch and mend that favorite, but worn out, pair of jeans in your closet. We will use embroidery, patchwork, shisiko, and other techniques to repair and embellish holes in clothing. Please bring garments you'd like to stitch upon, and all other supplies will be provided. All levels are welcome!

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Please bring garments you'd like to stitch upon, and all other supplies will be provided

item.title: No Rules Quilted iPad Case with Camille Perrin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Create a functional zippered case with scraps, unconventional shapes and designs. The piece is built one geometric segment at a time, installation of zipper completes the bag with an angle!

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Requirements are a sewing machine in good working order, lots of 100% cotton scraps, threads and bobbins that don't match, a 20 x 20 piece of fabric for the lining, a rotary cutter, mat and basic sewing tools. Instructor will supply fusible lining and zippers

item.title: The Marriage of Metal and Polymer Clay: Links with Lynn Yuhr
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
This workshop is part of a series called ‘Marriage of Metal and Polymer Clay’. The focus of these workshops is to introduce polymer artists to a simple, cold connection metalsmithing skills that will allow them to take their work to the next level.
Links are a way to provide points of connections in the construction of your jewelry. Most commonly, they are thought of as connections in a necklace, but they can just as easily be used in earring, bracelets and even brooches.
This class focuses on making simple links combining polymer clay and wire. Some of the basics when working with wire and polymer will be covered. For the wire, this includes work hardening, straightening, forming and whether to add a patina and when. For the polymer, this includes color blends, simple veneers, how thick to work, and baking tips. The polymer technique used for the veneers is stripes. They are fun, fast and bold - using bright colors to make each piece sing!
This class is being offered virtually over two days. Each day is 2 hours long. It is a demo-based class meaning that each step in the project will be reviewed, demonstrated and discussed but the making time is on your own, homework will be assigned between class.

item.title: Say it with Cardboard with Tyler K. Smith
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This workshop will utilize the simplicity of cardboard to explore the Design Elements, Principles, and techniques of sculpture. Following the traditional process of concept to finished piece, the material’s versatility allows for both, easily realized additive and reductive processes with a wide range of finishing options. There isn’t any single object that can’t be recreated in cardboard. This workshop is suitable for all skill levels. Talent is not required, just the need to express oneself... in cardboard!

item.title: 3D Design with Tyler K Smith
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This class will explore the Elements and Principles of Design, as well as a wide range of problem-solving strategies, in 3D. Each week, the course will introduce a new material that offers very interesting and unique ways of expressing an idea in sculptural form. All skill levels are welcome. As long as there is an idea to share, this class will find a way to tell it.

item.title: The Art of Cartooning with Tyler K Smith
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Narrative and sequential imagery has been used throughout history to imbue the visual arts with meaning.
From the single-panel cartoon to the multi-framed storyboard, The Art of Cartooning will look at the histories of illustration, picture book art, cartooning, comic book art, animation, and cinematic storyboards.
Starting with an image's basic function to dispense information, this studio art class will explore storytelling, personal styles, drawing mediums, character development, and layout. These aspects will encourage the development of the narrative and emotional range required to create meaningful, illustrated short stories.
We will explore and develop the act of seeing and how to infuse that act with style and personality in our drawing. We will explore the myriad of drawing techniques and mediums. We will always work within the fundamental canon of the Formal Design Elements and solid compositional Principles.
This workshop is open to all skill levels. Talent is not required. Talent is NOT the barometer of success. Having a personal vision, the need for something to say, is what truly matters.

item.title: Classical Approach to Still Life Painting with Barbara Cricchio-Efchak
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
This Still Life Oil Painting Class will focus on improving basic and advanced skills by understanding and conceptualizing the light effect on forms. The skills that we will focus on will be:
  • Drawing: using comparative measure
  • Composition: working on understanding how to create dynamic compositions
  • Value: Identify and develop the correct value, which is key to a successful painting
  • Hue: students will learn the discipline to mix color by using a pallet knife to create color strings to begin to control hue and value.
Each student will bring a variety of items they wish to include in a simple still life with the intention of completing a painting in eight weeks. Depending on the size of the class, either there will be two set ups or students can create their own. Curriculum:
  • Week 1- choose items to develop a pleasing and interesting composition. Develop a simple line drawing that is used to transfer the drawing to canvas.
  • Week 2 – Transfer drawing to toned canvas and begin grisaille underpainting to establish values.
  • Week 3 – mix strings of color and begin painting first layer
  • Week 4 – 8 oil out the painting and evaluate which areas of the painting need more development focusing on edges and detail. Depending on the complexity of the composition these paintings can be completed or can be developed further at home.
The instructor will both demonstrate each process and bring examples to show the class. Barbara will work with each student to help them with personal development, guiding them to advance their own skills based on their current skills.

item.title: Create Your Own Fused Glass Mask with Chelsea Rousso
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Unleash your creativity in this hands-on class where you'll design and craft a stunning fused glass mask that can be fully fused and slumped or left flat to be displayed.
Learn the basics of glass cutting, layering, and kiln-firing techniques to bring your unique vision to life. Perfect for beginners and experienced artists alike, this workshop blends artistry and craftsmanship to produce a one-of-a-kind decorative or wearable piece.
All materials and tools provided!

item.title: Fused Glass Hearts with Stacy Gates
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Love is in the air
In this beginner friendly workshop, students will first look at design ideas and learn how to score and cut glass using multiple tools. Each student will be given a 4" glass heart base that has been cut for them using the studio's ring saw. They will then be able to create their individual design on top of the base using a combination of sheet glass, frit, stringers, dots and decorative murrini. Upon completion, the hearts will be fired in the studio's glass kiln and should be ready for pick up within a week.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Materials and firing schedules are included with additional materials and firings available for purchase. Please wear closed toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.

item.title: Stacking Rings & Bezel Cup Setting with Ace Tilton Ratcliff
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: During this three hour workshop, students will create three beautiful sterling silver textured wire rings—one with a cabochon stone setting! Everyone will learn how to size and solder a ring, as well as set a stone in a bezel cup. All materials are included, and no experience is required.

item.title: Creative Figure Drawing Workshop with Fernando Porras
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Learn to draw expressive figures with ease from a live model. This workshop will explore the figure’s basic structure to develop beautiful designs using a number of fun and creative shading finishes for both the figure and the background. The first session will emphasize composition, quick sketching techniques, negative spaces, and the structure of the figure, while the second session will show how to use light and diverse shading techniques to create volumes that jump off the page.

item.title: Intermediate to Advanced Jewelry & Metalsmithing (Wednesday)
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Advance your jewelry fabrication skills by expanding your knowledge of soldering, forming, and creating mechanisms to make beautiful bracelets, rings, and/or pendants. Demonstrations will include constructing box clasps, hinges, and hollow forms using copper and/or silver. Students will develop their own designs to create one-of-a-kind pieces. Use of the jeweler's saw, drilling, and some experience with soldering is necessary.

item.title: Silver Clay Jewelry with Glass Stones with Marthe Harwell
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Students will select beautiful, fused glass pieces resembling cabochon stones and fire them into silver clay to make a unique, one-of-a-kind pendant. Various application methods will be applied using solid and syringe silver clay to capture your sparkly stone in real silver!
ALL materials and firing schedules are supplied for this workshop. Please wear closed toes shoes, comfortable clothes, and an apron (if you have one).

item.title: Origami Butterfly Workshop with John Wienke
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Come create Origami Base Butterflies.
This course uses the Michael LaFosse and Richard Alexander’s technique to fold origami butterflies.
All supplies are included.

item.title: The Nude Figure in Oil with Fernando Porras
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Learn to create beautiful contemporary nude figures in oil. This two-day workshop will explore the nude female figure and the use of different color palette compositions to portray light, volumes, and emotions. The first morning will start with oil technique demonstrations and color theory and composition exercises to help you develop an idea for your piece. The instructor will work with you for the remainder of the workshop to help you create a composition based on a live model, and guide you through the process of mixing and applying oils to your canvas using a variety of techniques and tools.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• 1 pre-stretched canvas. Recommended approximate size: 16” x 20”
  • Medium-sized oil brushes. Choose your preferred shape and size. At least one 1-inch flat brush recommended. A basic oil color set is recommended. Main suppliers offer color sets of 10 tubes (37ml) that can be ordered online.
  • I will be using the following colors (Please keep in mind that some other similar colors that you might already have will surely work perfectly, too):
    • Burnt Sienna
    • Van Dyke Brown
    • Prussian Blue (using a French ultramarine, phthalo blue, or similar will be OK)
    • Cerulean Blue or similar
    • Cadmium-Free Orange or similar Cadmium-Free Yellow or Chrome Yellow Hue or similar
    • Cadmium-Free Red (or other medium reds work, too)
    • Magenta (Quinacridone Deep Pink or similar will be OK)
    • Payne’s Gray (Charcoal Gray or other blacks work, too)
    • Soft Mixing White (Titanium white or other whites ok, too)
  • Sketching pencils
  • White eraser and a kneaded eraser
  • Sketching paper (A few sheets of regular bond printer paper will do)
  • To thin my paints, I'll be using Odorless Turpenoid – turpentine substitute (Odorless), from Weber. • To clean your brushes, definitely consider the odorless and non-toxic Turpenoid Natural brush cleaner brand.

item.title: Textured Pendant with a Stone with Taylor Gigante
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this workshop, students will learn how to apply various hammered textures and stamping techniques to create a beautiful surface to their pendant. Once everyone has textured their surfaces, students will use the torch to solder a bezel cup which will be used for setting a stone. No experience is required and ALL materials are included!

item.title: Embroidery & Embellishments with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Bring jeans, dish towels, button down shirts, denim jackets, and miniskirts to this fun and fashionable fiber art workshop. Learn simple ways to embellish your wardrobe by adding beaded and embroidered accents to your clothing! Make one of a kind threads that express your unique personality. Learn embroidery stitches and hand sewing skills, laugh, and relax in this fun and creative workshop for free-spirited clothes horses. All tastes can be accommodated. This beginner-friendly workshop will approach the basics of the fiber arts, including using hand-sewing tools and techniques, in a fun and accessible way. Please bring a personal fabric item (non-stretchy) to embellish with embroidery and beads. And get ready to rock.

item.title: Fabrics Galore! Art Collage with Camille Perrin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Learn to make outrageous designs with or without a sewing machine! No sew applique uses lightweight fusible web and your pattern pieces cut and stacked to create birds, fish, animals, florals or abstracts.
The pieces will be cut, numbered and assembled in sequence to create a dimensional appliqued work of art.
This masterpiece can be further embellished with buttons, jewels and whatever sparks your imagination. Students can use their own designs or use designs supplied by the instructor.

item.title: Endless Possibilities with Amaco with Zoë Hall
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This workshop will overview AMACO’s mid-range (cone 5 / 6) glazes & underglazes! Including Potters Choice, Potters Choice Flux, Celadons & Velvet Underglazes. Images, features & benefits, application and firing tips will be shared. Attendees can test and experiment with new PCs, PCFs and UGs on their own wares or test tiles. Participants should bring up to 6 small bisque pieces (no more than 5” tall 4” wide), bisque test tiles (must be cone 6 or cone 10 clays) brushes and a notebook.

item.title: Fused Glass Lanterns with Stacy Gates
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase. In this one-day workshop students will be designing and creating 4 decorated glass panels to replace the plain glass supplied in a store-bought lantern.
This workshop is perfect for all levels of experience. Create 4 decorated glass panels to replace the plain glass supplied in a store bought lantern. Students will begin the day by learning about the different tools and types of glass used in glass fusing and you will learn to cut glass with confidence. After the basics, we will focus on coming up with design ideas for your panels - some ideas are florals, seasons, geometric, plants and variations of an object. The sample lantern has different sailboats on each panel. spend the afternoon making our lantern panels.
The workshop fee includes all tools and supplies, including your lantern. Please wear closed toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.
Email Carolyn Austin with any question at Carolyn@lighthousearts.org

item.title: Swiftie Swag
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: FLORIDA!! Swiftie Swag   Alright Swifties, let’s make some original fan swag while listening to our favorite songs!!  During this workshop, we’ll learn how to dye a t-shirt in our favorite pastel colors.  After making our awesome one-of-a-kind shirts, we will make our friendship bracelets as well as a pendant or pair of earrings.  Join us this summer for a great time making art with fellow swifties!  We ask you to bring a white cotton t-shirt that you’d like to use for the dying process. All other supplies are included!

item.title: Intro to Fiber Arts with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Discover various fabrics and fibers to create a colorful relief perfect for brightening up a room! Demonstrations will include embroidery stitching and hand sewing techniques, use of water-soluble substrate, and developing effective layering.  We will use fiber dying methods and inclusions to spice up your composition!  NO experience is necessary.  Materials are included!

item.title: Fused Faux Woven Hearts with Jen Rubinstein
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Create a fused glass heart to share or keep for yourself. In this workshop students will learn to score and cut strips of glass using multiple tools. You will be given a pre-cut heart-shaped glass base to build upon with your glass strips and a variety of accessory glass pieces. Design considerations will be discussed. This workshop is suitable for beginners. Please wear close-toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron if you like. Materials and firing schedules are included with additional materials and firings schedules available for purchase. Email Carolyn with any questions at: Carolyn@lighthousearts.org

item.title: Intro to Jewelry with Ace Tilton Ratcliff
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Students will be introduced to the fundamentals of metalsmithing through instructor demonstrations, one-on-one instruction, and hands-on experience with hand tools, flex shafts, and torches. Each student will learn to design, pierce, drill, solder, and set a cabochon stone. Students will work with sterling silver, brass, and/or copper throughout this course and projects will include making rings, pendants, and/or earrings.​ Projects include a textured band ring with a handmade bezel setting, pasting an image to sheet metal and piercing it out with a jeweler's saw to make a pendant, basic soldering including sweat soldering, and creating a necklace pendant using either a bezel or a prong setting.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
Materials are provided the first day of class.
Lisa will discuss the items below for you to order before the second class.
Herkules White Label #2/0 Saw Blade 1 dozen Sterling Silver 3” x 2” Sheet, 20-Ga., Dead-Soft, Brushed Finish Sterling Silver Round Wire, 16-Ga., Dead-Soft 1’ 6” Sterling Silver 1/4” Strip, 16-Ga., Dead-Soft 3”
We will discuss purchasing a round or oval cabochon stone for this class. You are welcome to bring one you already have, just make sure it is no smaller than 10mm.

item.title: Mother's Day Jewelry Workshop with Tracey Roedl
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Make mom a special sterling silver "Mom" station necklace. Using a jeweler's sawframe pierce (cut out) the Mom and attach it to a beautiful chain for Mom. Students will learn to pi their erce sterling sheet, file, sand, and hand polish the design to a mirror-finish or satin-finish. Students will take home finished gift for mom. Workshop includes all sterling silver sheet, clasp, and chain. Mother's Day Workshop

item.title: Teen Personal Expression with Caroline Duran
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Participants will choose a broad topic or theme to explore. We will practice organizing and developing artworks through concept design, symbolism, and sketching while focusing on artistic voice and vision. Hand-built sculptural or functional artwork can be created throughout the workshop. While this workshop will focus on form, surface options will be discussed. Themes:*Personal Experiences: Explore your own life, relationships, and cultural background.
  • *Social Commentary: Address issues or events that resonate with you.
  • *Abstract Concepts: Investigate ideas like time, space, or the human condition.
  • *Nature: Capture the beauty and power of the natural world.
  • *Everyday Objects: Find meaning and symbolism in ordinary items.
  • *Portraits: Explore the human form and character.
  • *Landscapes: Depict the beauty and vastness of the world around us.
  • *Still Life: Arrange and capture the beauty of inanimate objects.

item.title: Portrait in Clay with Caroline Duran
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: During this workshop participants will learn to look at the human figure objectively. We will model the eyes, nose, mouth, and ears. Each study will be built solid and hollowed out. After the anatomy studies are completed, a small scale, in the round portrait will be started. Reference photos of selected subject (side, front, and back) are required and are the responsibility of each participant. Photos should be clear, well-lit, and detailed. Ipads, laptops, or high-quality printed images are suggested. The instructor will offer an approach to portraiture that focuses on anatomical structure, mapping, proportion, and capturing the individuality of each subject.

item.title: Under the Sea with Caroline Duran
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This workshop provides a unique opportunity for a parent and child to work together to craft beautiful pots inspired by the sea. No prior clay experience is required - just bring an open mind and a desire to create! During the workshop, you and your child will each make a simple pinch pot and add hand-sculpted and sprig mold details inspired by under the sea elements.

item.title: Parent and Me: Sleepy Face Planters with Caroline Duran
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
These sleepy face planters provide the perfect loving home for your plants. Change the hairstyle your face planter is sporting by changing the plant. Every face is created by hand. No molds are used, so each of these lovely faces is one of a kind! Plant not provided.
$60 tuition includes Parent + Child

item.title: Wearable Words: Silver Necklace with Tracey Roedl
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Express yourself by turning your words into a sterling silver necklace. Learn to draw then pierce (cut) out your own signature using a jeweler's saw frame and sawblades on silver sheet. You will learn to achieve a mirror-finish and a satin-finish by hand (no polishing bits or drills needed). You'll add the chain to complete your necklace. All materials are included!

item.title: Charming Necklaces with Tracey Roedl
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Make a sterling silver charm necklace! Learn to pierce (cut) out your shape with a jeweler’s saw frame and sawblades using sterling silver sheet. Learn techniques to file, sand, and polish to a professional mirror-finish by hand (no equip. needed). We will attach the chain to complete. All materials are included!

item.title: Teen Potter's Wheel Workshop with Courtney Page
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Join us for a fun and immersive 2-day Teen clay workshop where you'll discover the fundamentals of the potter’s wheel! Learn how to shape and create beautiful vessels like cups and bowls, guided step-by-step through the wheel-throwing process. By the end of the workshop, each student will have 3–4 unique, handcrafted pieces that will be glazed and fired. (pick-up approx. weeks after completion of Workshop)   All materials are provided, and no prior experience is needed—just bring your creativity!

item.title: Diamond Necklace with Tracey Roedl
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Bling, bling! In this workshop, students will make a stunning sterling silver pendant with a Herkimer Diamond (a crystal-clear natural quartz crystal). Using a jeweler's saw frame and sawblades you will pierce (cut) out the outside shape of your choice and then at the center pierce out the prongs that hold the stone. Then you file and sand the silver, set the crystal and add the chain.
*Some believe the energy of these stones will guide you through difficult situations and put you at ease. They are thought to make your work vision clear and help manifest dreams.

item.title: Portraits in Clay with Caroline Duran
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This course teaches students to create ready-to-fire clay bust/figures using reference photos and solid-building techniques. Through demonstrations and individual instruction, students will sculpt facial features, explore expression and gesture, and develop a personal concept for their piece. The course covers structural integrity, drying/firing methods, and surface finishing options like glazing or painting, providing a comprehensive foundation in portrait sculpture.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: All tools needed can by purchased at 3D Studio Artshop, finishing sponges, and modeling/large loop tools, bucket with lid (or Tupperware) for slip, t-shirts/black trash bags, serrated/rubber ribs (red/blue), wire cutter, various paint brushes, sketchbook (optional), laptop to view reference photos while sculpting Highly Recommended: Amazon.com: Xiem Tools Scraper Tool (Double-Ended) for Pottery and Ceramics Book 1: Portrait Sculpting: Anatomy & Expressions in Clay by Faraut - PCF Studios (philippefaraut.com)

item.title: Painting Poetry and Prose with Ruth Mamo
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Many of us are inspired by painting, poetry and prose because it has the ability to move and inspire us. Whether you are a casual reader or enjoy a rich reading life, join me in an invitation to explore painting through poetry and prose that moves and inspires you to a new level. Using watercolor, collage, ink and mixed media, journey into the world of inspired art allowing poetry and/or prose to be a muse for your painterly life. Through your choice of poetry, prose and art medium(s), you will be able to create a collection of art work in an inspired art journal. All level artists are welcome to join me in this gentle, open, workshop environment to celebrate and deepen your creative life

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
Mixed Media Art Journal
Paint Pencils
Collage materials

item.title: Radiant Arrangements: Designing with Many Stones with Lisa Johnson
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this class, we will arrange multiple faceted and nonfaceted stones in our jewelry designs to double the dazzle, triple the shine. Demonstrations will cover setting a faceted stone using prongs, tabs, and tube. Various bezel settings will also be introduced! Students must have experience with a jeweler’s saw and torch.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: The instructor will go over all materials with you on the first day of class. Prepare to spend approx. $50 for this 6-8 week class.

item.title: Stacked Squares and Beyond with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Great for advancing your glass cutting skills. This class will improve your cutting skills and the proper ways to stack a variety of sizes and colors of glass for a perfectly fused one of a kind dish or bowl. Learn how the different thickness and layout of the glass will form in the kiln, what type of reactions some glass may have wit each other in the heat and the proper fusing schedules that will be used to bring it all together! Not only will students be working with straight cuts and square shapes, but will create more advanced designs in a circular and curved pattern. The use of cold working tools will also be implemented in this class. Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase. Glass cutting skills recommended.
Closed toed shoes required.
Please Email at Carolyn@LighthouseArts.org with any questions.

item.title: Textiles in Fused Glass with Stacy Gates
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Celebrate the timeless beauty of traditional quilt blocks—reimagined in vibrant fused glass! In this hands-on workshop, students will explore the intersection of textile artistry and glasswork by selecting 3–4 classic quilt designs to translate into glass compositions.
Using simple geometric shapes like squares, rectangles, and triangles, you'll learn how to transform paper patterns into colorful, cohesive designs. Your finished work will be kiln-fused into either a square plate or a long platter, combining the charm of quilting with the brilliance of glass. Glass cutting experience required.
Join us and piece together something truly unique—no thread required!
Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase.
Closed toed shoes required
Email Carolyn with any questions at: Carolyn@LighthouseArts.org

item.title: Vitrigraph Stringers with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Learn to pull and draw with vitrigraph stringers. In this 4 week glass fusion class we will work with hot melted glass, pulling it from a Caldera kiln to make your own unique stringers. Combine them with a variety of other glass colors and frit to create glass bowls, dishes or wall art.
This technique is sure to amaze you! Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase
Closed toed shoes, cotton long sleeve shirts and cotton pants required.
Please Email at Carolyn@LighthouseArts.org with any questions

item.title: Youth Advanced Drawing Mixed Media with Maggie Jahn
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Looking to take your drawing to the next level? Experiment with different drawing media to communicate your ideas and passion. This class combines observational and imaginative drawing with process based mixed media techniques such as collage, oil pastel resist, watercolor pencil, trace monotype and more!

item.title: Introduction to Handbuilding in Clay with Zoe Lowenthal
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Through demonstrations and individualized instruction, students will learn the foundations of handbuilding by creating a pinch pot, a coil vase, and a slab-built vessel. Students will also learn about the stages of clay, attaching techniques, clay safety, proper storage methods, and concept development/sketching. This class will give students a comprehensive overview of the basics of sculpting with clay and the ideas central to creating compelling three-dimensional vessels and sculptures. No previous clay experience is required.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Notebook with pencil, Basic Clay tools, beginner clay tool kit can be purchased at 3D Studio ArtShop. Optional: Apron, Small hand towel.

item.title: Functional Furry Friend Forms with Caroline Duran
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: During this class, students will learn how to create functional hand-built vessels that feature your favorite furry friends! Techniques that will be explored include building with slabs, additive relief methods, and subtractive carving methods. Surfacing principles that will be discussed include functional vs. decorative surfaces, the importance of  transparency/opacity, best practices of glazing/underglazing, cone numbers and firing, and the use of oxides/stains/washes to highlight texture. Test tiles are highly encouraged for experimentation with various surface methods. Students will aim to execute 2-3 finished vessels to be fired and glazed within the session. No hand-building or sculpting experience required, all levels welcome!

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Supplies: sponges, mini and standard loop tools for hollowing and carving, needle tool, scoring tool, clay knife or x-acto knife, small Tupperware for slip, soft rubber ribs (red/blue), wire cutter, various paint brushes, wooden modeling tool, sketchbook to plan and make glazing notes (optional) laptop or Ipad required daily to view reference photos while sculpting), modeling tools for sculpting and carving 25 lbs of clay included

item.title: Artsy Apron with Kate Gouery
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Cooking, grilling, ceramics, painting, and other creative activities require an apron! Make your apron stand out with Lino-block printing! The first day will include creating our blocks. The second day we will put our blocks into action! Whether it’s for yourself or a gift to another, this is sure to be a hit! An apron will be supplied as well as all materials. If you decide to do another apron, please purchase cotton. No experience is required to take this class.

item.title: Beginning Collage Quilting with Camille Perrin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This workshop is designed to explore the principals of color, value, and shading in the process of developing a fabric collage. This is a raw edge quilting piece, and no machine is necessary. An image (cat, duck, a skull, mushroom and several others) will be provided in grey tones that will then be interpreted in color, texture, and shapes. Students who have experience painting will find this to be a new, exciting way of developing wall art. Great fun, simple, and fabulous results! Colors are assembled as to a preferred pallet; shapes are cut and assembled to the foundation panel. A simple collage will be created first to establish the basics, moving towards a more complex composition.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• Colored fabrics,
    • 100% cotton,
  • scissors.
  • Lite Steam a Seam 2
  • Parchment paper
  • ¼ inch foam core board covered in white felt,
    • 24 x 24 is a good size.
  • Pins,
  • tweezers,
  • good scissors, large and small Cotton fabrics
    • an assortment of colors,
    • batiks are great for fabric collage
  • Mini iron

item.title: Intro to Alcohol Ink with Alene Sirott-Cope
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This introductory workshop illustrates the ease and fun of creating your own custom ceramic tiles for back splashes, kitchen and bathroom accents, trivets, coasters, wall hangings and more. Learn by playing with the inks for the first hour to get the “feel”. 4 demos will guide the student through the steps to creating a final landscape. The last tile will involve stamping on a creative background. Students will work with white ceramic bathroom tiles, using household items to create with, including paper towels, Q tips, gauze, felt, rags, coffee stirrers, cotton balls, old credit cards. (see materials list). You do not have to be an artist to enjoy this class.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: • paper towels • Q_tips • gauze • felt square • rags • coffee stirrers, • cotton balls • old credit card • 91% isopropyl alcohol • 3-5 different colors of alcohol ink, any brand to start. Green, Blue, Yellow, brown. suggested • Spray bottle. small (for alcohol) • 5-10 white bathroom tiles • favorite rubber stamp • I will supply extras if needed

item.title: Palm Bleach Splatters with Jenna Hoefert
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Get your Palm Bleach look this season! In this workshop, students will take a black cotton t-shirt provided by the Lighthouse ArtCenter and apply a variety of bleach applications that will leave an amazing impression. Surface splatters will be made using palm fronds, leaves, spray bottles, sand, pebbles, etc.. Make sure to wear OLD clothes & shoes during this workshop as it is highly possible that you may get bleach on yourself. This workshop will be held outside. Contact Lisaj@lighthousearts.org to give your t-shirt size.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Contact Lisaj@lighthousearts.org to give your t-shirt size.

item.title: Stitched Designs & Shibori for Everyone! with Jenna Hoefert
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Shibori is a traditional Japanese dyeing technique that uses indigo. During this workshop, students will create beautiful hand sewn and/or machine sewn patterns to develop a resist for an incredible surface design once dyed in the indigo. Please bring a light weight, drapey white cotton blouse, tank top, cover up, bandana etc.. You are welcome to bring a sewing machine, but it is not required. ALL other materials are supplied. No experience is required!

item.title: Ice Cool Dyes, Hot Colors! with Jenna Hoefert
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Get into Florida beach mode by making your own fun, colorful rayon sarong and soft, V-neck t-shirt! Students will use an Ice-Dyeing technique to develop beautiful surfaces on their garment of choice. Colors will separate and stratify making for a lovely watercolor effect. Garments are ordered by the Lighthouse ArtCenter. Please contact lisaj@lighthousearts.org to let us know your size! ALL materials are included. No experience is required. You will need to pick up your items the following week due to the dyeing process.

item.title: Marbling Glass Ornaments and Paper Cards with Peggy Wertheim
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Fun, Easy and Inspiring! Yes, Marbling with acrylics on carrageenen will inspire you with instant gratification and success! Peggy teaches Traditional Marbling techniques for you to create DECORATIVE GLASS BAUBLES ORNAMENTS. You will create 10 One-of-a-Kind Glass Beauties PLUS marbled papers with envelopes too! Bring your love of art, your creativity & your curiosity – everything else is included.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: All included! 10 glass ornaments, papers & envelopes, and all the conumables.

item.title: No Sew Quirky Quilting with Camille Perrin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Applique Collage uses lightweight fusible bonding material and all the brightly colored scraps you can find! Batiks are wonderful for this. Your design will be created entirely from shapes and colors cut, numbered and assembled in sequence -then secured to your backing material. The finished piece can be stitched, embellished with buttons, jewels or backing material. Whatever sparks your imagination.
Students are encouraged to create their own designs or use designs supplied by the instructor.
No machines, just your imagination, brightly colored scraps, a 20 x 20 piece of fabric. Bring a good pair of scissors if you have them.

item.title: Contemporary Limoges Enameling – Painting with Fire with Mi-Sook Hur
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Discover the luminous art of Limoges enameling in this dynamic, hands-on workshop. Participants will learn essential techniques—sifting, wet-packing, firing, and layering—while bringing vivid, nature-inspired subjects like flowers, bees, and butterflies to life.
Through guided demos, the class will explore overglaze painting, mastering the interplay of color, light/dark, and tone to create striking, realistic effects. By the end, participants will complete a series of small enamel pieces perfect for rings, earrings, or pendants.
No prior experience needed—just creativity and curiosity!

Please wait to order materials until we have confirmed the workshop has met minimum enrollment by Nov. item.title: Terra Sig, Coil and Pinch with Kate Marotz
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this workshop, participants will learn how to create sculptural pots for daily use through utilizing a coil and pinch technique. Kate will also demonstrate how she creates her surfaces with terra sigillata, wax resist, and a wash. Participants will hand-build cups, mugs, or bowls of their own design and plan their surface decoration. The first two days of the workshop will focus primarily on the coil and pinch technique, but towards the end of the second day terra sigillata will be introduced. Any pots that are bone dry for the third day will be decorated with terra sigillata, Kate will then demonstrate the steps she completes between the bisque and glaze firings.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• Scoring Tool
  • X-acto knife

item.title: Master Workshop: Human Portrait with Eduardo Gomez
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
The workshop will cover basic anatomy of the head and anatomical proportions. It will also cover anatomical issues related to aging and race and facial expressions. It will teach students how to use the shape and the planes of the face to obtain a general likeness. We will also study different ways of modeling the individual parts such as the nose, lips, ears and eyes. Certain surface finishing techniques will also be covered.
The class will also cover basic design issues involved in designing a bust sculpture as well as how to prepare it for firing or molding, and different mounting options. Workshop includes 25lbs of clay and one bisque firing.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Basic personal clay tools, Beginners Clay Kit that can be purchased at 3D Studio, Apron.

item.title: Master Workshop: Bas Relief with Eduardo Gomez
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Use your mark making techniques on clay and learn the secrets of combining your drawing and sculpting skills to make bas relief sculpture (aka low relief). Each student is asked to provide source imagery for sculpting for example; photo of a family dog or an interesting magazine clip of a garden. Images should be around 8 ½ by 11 in. This class is designed to be taken in conjunction with the follow week’s workshop, Molding and Cold Cast your Bas Relief. No previous sculpture experience required, but some drawing proficiency is recommended. This Workshop includes 25lbs of clay and one bisque firing.

item.title: Master Workshop: Relaxing Figure with Model with Eduardo Gomez
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Students will cover basic anatomy of the head, body and anatomical proportions by observing a live model. We will cover issues related to design and mounting of the sculpture. We will also study different ways of modeling the individual parts such as the hands and feet nose, lips, ears and eyes. Certain surface finishing techniques will also be covered. The class will cover how to hollow the sculpture to get it ready for firing. 25 lbs of clay included and one firing.

item.title: Master Workshop: The Standing Figure (Armature and Plasticine) with Eduardo Gomez
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This workshop is designed for more advanced students who are interest or curious about casting their sculptures in bronze. Using a live model, the students will sculpt a full figure sculpture in a standing position using plasteline oil-based clay. This clay does not dry or shrink, thereby preventing cracking when used on a metal armature, enabling the sculptor to create thin body parts such as arms, legs, hands and fingers as well as flowing open poses. Beyond the Workshop: Since the sculpture cannot be fired this piece will need to be taken to a foundry so that molds can be made and used to make a lost wax casting. The instructor will consider organizing a day trip to the foundry for those who are interested. The fee for this will be separate from the workshop. The costs of the foundry work as well as the supervision of the work therein, will be the responsibility of each student.

item.title: It's OK, I Fixed It! Mending Workshop with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Give beloved, well-worn belongings new life with this fun and creative hand sewing workshop! Learn different ways to visibly patch and mend that favorite, but worn out, pair of jeans in your closet. We will use embroidery, patchwork, shisiko, and other techniques to repair and embellish holes in clothing. Please bring garments you'd like to stitch upon, and all other supplies will be provided. All levels are welcome!

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Bring in something that needs to be mended! We got the rest.

item.title: Thankful Times Together: Personal Photo Decor with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Happy Thanksgiving!! Join the slow-stitching movement! Or, refresh your memory of an old, favorite hobby with this non-traditional embroidery workshop. Learn fresh, or brush up, on sewing basics in a zero-judgment zone! Go home with a hand-sewn sample of stitchery that doubles as a ready-to-hang a piece of art featuring your closest loved ones. With group demos and one-on-one help, students will work at their level with different beads, fabrics, flosses, hoops, needles, notions, and even disappearing ink! Embroidery stitches, bead-work, and other embellishment techniques will be taught to create small, quick, and easy pieces for the home, or to give as a gift. Designs rotate seasonally and are always changing!

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Bring photos of your family or loved ones to incorporate into your project! Smaller photos will work best

item.title: Fabric of my Heart Collage with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Look like a domestic goddess and learn how to create easy, hand-sewn collages! These simple, colorful designs can be mounted to a greeting card and sent as happy mail. They can be matted and framed, or hung on the wall, as-is. This beginner-friendly workshop will approach the basics of fiber art and sewing in a fun (promise) and accessible way.
Using just a few stitches (literally), a handful of fabric scraps, and some sticker-backed fabric that disappears in water, students will create textile collages of florals, animals, landscapes, and other simple shapes. Matted collages can be framed, hung on walls, or given as gifts.
Designs will rotate seasonally and can be adapted to meet the needs of every student.
All levels of expertise are welcome. Come play with needles and thread in a low-pressure environment. With jokes.

item.title: New Year, New Sparkle: Upcycled Jewelry Collage with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: It's time to shine! Give old, broken, discarded amazing costume jewelry new life by creating easy, hand-sewn, cheerful collages! This beginner-friendly workshop will approach the basics of collage art and hand sewing in a fun (promise) and accessible way. Using just a few stitches (literally) and a handful of sparkle, we'll create collages of Your favorite drink, florals, animals, and other simple shapes. Matted collages can be framed, hung on walls, or given as gifts. Designs will rotate seasonally and can be adapted to meet the needs of every student. All levels of expertise are welcome. Come play with needles and thread in a low-pressure environment.

item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Bring jeans, dish towels, button down shirts, denim jackets, and miniskirts to this fun and fashionable fiber art workshop. Learn simple ways to embellish your wardrobe by adding beaded and embroidered accents to your clothing! Make one of a kind threads that express your unique personality. Learn embroidery stitches and hand sewing skills, laugh, and relax in this fun and creative workshop for free-spirited clothes horses. All tastes can be accommodated. This beginner-friendly workshop will approach the basics of the fiber arts, including using hand-sewing tools and techniques, in a fun and accessible way. Please bring a personal fabric item (non-stretchy) to embellish with embroidery and beads. And get ready to rock.

item.title: Telescope Tees with Jenna Hoefert
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Join us for an out of this world experience dyeing T-shirts inspired by NASA photos from James Webb & Hubble Telescopes! Students will apply low-immersion dye to make marvelous, colorful shirts with outer space in mind for themselves or someone else.

item.title: Ceramic Furniture (Think Big, Build Small) with Casey Zablocki
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
In this two-day workshop, students will be encouraged to think big—conceptualizing a piece or series of ceramic furniture they’d love to create. From that big idea, they’ll bring it to life on a smaller scale by building a maquette.
I will guide students through various handbuilding techniques—primarily slabs and coils—while demonstrating different materials, building methods, and firing processes, along with the unique benefits of each approach.
This is a hands-on, exploratory workshop designed to equip students with the tools and confidence to transform ambitious ideas into physical form. With these techniques, the possibilities are endless.

item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Create your own unique Holiday ornaments, suncatchers or gift tags to decorate your home or gift to others. You will learn the basics of glass fusion using a variety of colored glass pieces, frit and stringers to make hanging ornaments or gift tags.
Children under 16 must have an adult registered with them
The workshop will run in 2 Hour Sessions Please choose a time slot when registering

item.title: Walk on Art with Lisa MacNamara
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Art on the Floor: Stand on Your Art, oh no! Create vibrant, functional art pieces designed to be walked on— an unexpected way to experience your own artwork!! In this hands-on workshop, you’ll design and paint a decorative floor covering on canvas, perfect for indoor or outdoor use. Learn techniques for binding, priming, and sealing your work for durability and even water resistance. Choose your size, from a smaller size, 24” x 12” for Fido’s water bowl or 3’x 5’ welcome home piece to make a statement- transform your art into a piece you can truly step into! Please note: if you desire a bigger size, please contact me.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Duck cloth canvas Acrylic paints – even interior satin house paint works! Your favorite image or designs Your favorite repeating pattern – bring examples of patterns you like

item.title: Abstracting the Figure: Water Color with Lisa MacNamara
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this expressive class designed for adults of all skill levels, students will learn to deconstruct the human figure into its essential shapes using watercolor's fluid and spontaneous nature. Through guided exercises and individual exploration, participants will study the figure and translate it into abstract compositions, focusing on line, color, form, and gesture rather than realistic detail. This class encourages creative interpretation, helping students develop their voice while expanding their understanding of abstraction and the expressive potential of watercolor. No prior figure drawing experience necessary—just a willingness to loosen up and explore!

item.title: Features of the iPhone Camera with Mark Stall
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Spend two hours learning more about your iPhone camera. Mark can guarantee, no one will leave without learning dozens of new techniques. Mark’s "Features of the iPhone Camera" will empower you to do more than you ever thought while improving your everyday photography. Learn the best camera settings so you’re always ready to capture the next image or video. Mark demonstrates the features of each camera, from Panoramic to Time-lapse videos. You’ll then move on to the Photos app, a powerful editor and catalog included with every iPhone. Mark’s workshop includes a follow-along handout & an extensive list of links to learn more about iPhone photography. All you need is your iPhone & the desire to continue to learn the specifics once you leave.

Any Apple iPhone smartphone & most current iOS
Pen for notes.

item.title: Editing your iPhone Photos with Mark Stall
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Snapseed is ‘’The Must-Have Mobile Editing App.’’
Join Mark for a hands-on workshop designed for photographers of all levels who want faster, smarter ways to edit their photos. You’ll leave with new tools, new techniques, and new inspiration. Snapseed is a free app for both iPhone & Androids.
  • Snapseed is simple, powerful, and surprisingly addictive. In Mark’s session, you'll:
  • Master a mobile editing workflow you can use every day.
  • Discover how to turn ordinary phone images into frame-worthy art
  • Learn to use healing, selective edits, & perspective correction with ease
  • Discover why Snapseed is a secret weapon for serious photographers
Participants should have a good understanding of their iPhones or Android phones and want to use it to edit their photo captures.
