item.title: Making Supermarket Flowers into a Professional-looking Design with Yvette Shakespeare
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Students will learn how : To buy flowers at the supermarket (What to look for and what to avoid) To condition flowers, maximizing their hydration in order to last longer To use the principles and elements of design To create a unique and professional looking flower arrangement to take home The instructor will demonstrate and teach for the first part of the workshop and then students will create their own design as the instructor goes around helping where needed. No experience is needed however one must have an enthusiasm for flowers

item.title: Terrarium Workshop with Jennifer Vasallo
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Hands on terrarium workshop where participants build their own self- sustaining ecosystem in glass. Students learn about plant care, substrate layering and the natural water cycle while creating a unique piece of living decor to take home. The workshop teaches the step by step technique of layering soil, charcoal and drainage along with planting and moss placement to create a balanced self-sustaining terrarium. All materials will be included .

item.title: Marbling Glass Ornaments or Baubles with Peggy Wertheim

item.title: Saggar Forms and Firing with Barbara Powell
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Join us for a two-day Saggar Firing workshop held over two consecutive weeks. The first session will focus on instruction and creating your wheel-thrown or hand-built pieces. After a bisque firing during the week, we’ll reconvene on the second day to explore the firing process in depth. This hands-on class will guide you through every step of the Saggar Firing method, an exciting alternative firing technique. Topics include designing forms suited for saggar, trimming and preparing greenware, applying saggar materials, and understanding the firing, reduction, and finishing stages.
2-Day WS Dates: Nov. 8th and Nov. 15th , 10-4pm (same WS both Saturdays)

item.title: Paint Your Home with Caroline Duran
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This workshop is accessible for levels from beginner to intermediate and is perfect for those seeking personal instruction. Learn how to paint a watercolor home portrait including the sky and landscape. Instructor will demonstrate layering colors and assist each student in the painting process from start to finish.

item.title: Flower Arrangement Demo with Yvette Shakespeare
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Yvette Shakespeare will give an exclusive talk and demonstration during Art in Bloom, showing you how to create a stunning flower arrangement using grocery store flowers, perfect for a holiday centerpiece or a thoughtful hostess gift. She’ll also share tips on how to care for and maintain your arrangement so it lasts as long as possible.

item.title: Thanksgiving Floral Bouquets with Creative Florals
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Celebrate the season of gratitude with a hands-on floral design workshop! Create your own beautiful Thanksgiving bouquet bursting with autumn blooms, rich textures, and warm harvest colors. Guided by Creative Florals, you’ll learn arranging techniques and tips for combining seasonal flowers and foliage into a stunning centerpiece — perfect for your holiday table or as a heartfelt gift. All materials are provided, and no experience is necessary — just bring your creativity and festive spirit!

item.title: Coloring Outside the Lines: Freeform Embroidery with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Once you know the basics, you can break the rules a little bit! Bring your imagination and learn how to increase the impact each stitch has upon your work in this freeform embroidery workshop. Stitch inconsistently, dynamically, irregularly, and do it on purpose! Maybe even add a little bling. This class is part study in line quality, using thread in lieu of pencil or pen, and part study in color theory, using different fibers of varying weight and value to achieve depth of field. For stitchers with some embroidery experience, each student will leave with a piece of original, handsewn, ready-to-hang, hoop art.

item.title: Slow-Stitch a ‘scape with Kerri On
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Build a deep & textured, vibrant, fabric collage that explodes out of its mat over the course of this four-week fiber art class. Starting with a blank canvas of fabric, we will use the latest products, tools & tricks of the trade to create one of a kind, hand-dyed, handsewn, seascapes & landscapes that teem with intricate, unique components. This class is for intermediate and advanced stitchers. Each student will leave with a matted, framed, ready to hang textile collage.

item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Great for Beginners and a fun night out with friends and family! Try your hand at Glass Fusion. In this mini-workshop, you will learn how to assemble and properly lay out a pattern using a variety of colored glass, frit, and stingers to create a one-of-a-kind decorative and functional glass dish in a comfortable relaxed atmosphere.
Students 12-18 years of age require a guardian 21 years of age plus.
Please wear closed-toed shoes, comfortable clothes, and an apron if you like.
All materials and firings included.

item.title: Fabric Collage for Beginners: Painting with Cloth with Camille Perrin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This workshop is designed to explore the principals of color, value, and shading in the process of developing a fabric collage. This is a raw edge quilting piece, and no machine is necessary. An image (cat, duck, a skull, mushroom and several others) will be provided in grey tones that will then be interpreted in color, texture, and shapes. Students who have experience painting will find this to be a new, exciting way of developing wall art. Great fun, simple, and fabulous results! Colors are assembled as to a preferred pallet; shapes are cut and assembled to the foundation panel. A simple collage will be created first to establish the basics, moving towards a more complex composition.

No machines, just your imagination, brightly colored scraps, a 20 x 20 piece of fabric.The LAC has plenty of scraps for everyone to use.

item.title: Vibrant Landscapes in Watermedia or Oil with Lyudmila Tomova Clark
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Embark on a colorful journey into the world of vibrant landscape painting, where the beauty of nature comes alive on canvas. Led by acclaimed artist Lyudmila Tomova Clark, a.k.a. Lucy, this workshop invites you to explore the dynamic interplay of color, light, and form, as you learn to capture the essence of landscapes with energy and expression.
Designed for artists of all levels, this workshop offers a hands-on exploration of techniques to infuse your landscapes with vibrancy and life. Whether you prefer watercolor, acrylic, or oil, you'll discover how to use color boldly and confidently to evoke mood, atmosphere, and emotion in your artwork.
Under Lyudmila's expert guidance, you'll learn to see the world with fresh eyes, find inspiration in the vivid hues of nature and translating them onto your canvas with passion and creativity. From marinas and cityscapes to intimate scenes, you'll learn to create compelling compositions that draw viewers into your world and leave a lasting impression.
The workshop will begin with a demonstration by Lyudmila, showcasing techniques for creating vibrant landscapes that pop with color and energy. You'll then put these techniques into practice, receiving personalized feedback and guidance from Lyudmila as you work on your own projects.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
Recommended Supply List

For this class, you may work in either oil or watercolor. Please review the supply list for your chosen medium below and bring the items that apply to that medium.

Option 1: Oil Painting Supplies

Painting Surface

  • Please bring a few stretched canvases or canvas panels, 11x14" or larger.
  • Choose a size that feels comfortable to you, but keep it under 18x24" for class.

Paints

Any brand you prefer is fine, but be sure to have a well-rounded palette of colors. Recommended colors:
  • Titanium White
  • Naples Yellow
  • Cadmium Yellow Medium
  • Lemon Yellow
  • Yellow Ochre
  • Cadmium Red
  • Orange
  • Alizarin Crimson
  • Burnt Umber
  • Ultramarine Blue
  • Prussian Blue
  • Turquoise
  • Sap Green
  • Ivory Black

Palette

  • A flat surface palette with enough space for mixing colors.

Brushes

A good variety will give you the most flexibility. Please include:
  • 2" large flat
  • Large, medium, and small rounds
  • Flats, brights, filberts, and angled brushes
  • Rigger brush for fine lines

Palette Knives

  • At least one palette knife is recommended (available at Jerry’s Artarama and most art supply stores).

Paper Towels

  • Essential for cleaning brushes and managing paint.

Medium

  • Please use an odorless, non-toxic oil painting medium.
  • You can find options listed under: Non-Toxic Oil Painting Supplies.

Option 2: Watercolor Supplies

Paper

  • Bring your favorite watercolor paper in a size you feel comfortable with.
  • Recommended: cold press, 140lb or 300lb, for a textured, absorbent surface that’s excellent for soft edges and expressive washes.
  • Hot press paper has a smooth, dense surface that’s better for crisp details, fine lines, and lifting.
  • Suggested sizes: 9x12", 11x15", or 12x16".
  • Please be prepared to complete about three paintings per day.
  • Reliable brands include: Arches, Fabriano, Saunders, Strathmore, and Canson.

Board

  • A sturdy board (Masonite or gator board) the same size or slightly larger than your paper is helpful for taping down your sheets.
  • Since we’ll mainly be working at tables, this may not always be necessary, but if you prefer using an easel, a solid backing is essential.

Paint

  • Any brand you enjoy is fine as long as you bring a good basic palette of colors.
  • Tubes are preferred because they allow you to use generous amounts for larger washes.
  • Daniel Smith paints are excellent.
  • If you’re on a budget, the Turner Watercolor set from Jerry’s Artarama is a great option.

Masking Fluid (Optional)

  • Useful for preserving the white areas of your paper.

Palette

  • Be sure to have a mixing area large enough for blending colors.
  • The Guerrilla Painter Backpacker Watercolor Palette (available at Jerry’s) is a solid choice.

Brushes

At minimum, bring three good-quality soft brushes with a fine point:
  • Large (for washes)
  • Medium (for general work)
  • Small (for details)
Additionally recommended:
  • 2" soft flat brush for bold washes
  • Rigger brush for fine lines and calligraphic strokes

Paper Towels

  • Essential for lifting paint, controlling moisture, and keeping brushes clean.

Spray Bottle (Optional)

  • Handy for rewetting paints or creating special effects.

Water Container

  • Bring a sturdy container for rinsing brushes.

item.title: Traditional Marbling: Two Scarves & Papers with Peggy Wertheim
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Unlike many Art Forms which take years to master, marbling will inspire you with instant gratification and success! Peggy will teach traditional marbling techniques using carrageenan and acrylic marbling paints on paper & silk. You will learn patterns of Feather, Bird Wing, Chevron & Peacock to create marbled papers and Two Silk Scarves. After the workshop, you can incorporate your beautiful new marbled papers into greeting cards, scrapbooking, collages, framed art, journal covers and so much more. Reference books & handout packet provided.
Bring your love of art, your creativity & your curiosity – everything else is included.

item.title: Traditional Marbling: One Scarf and Papers with Peggy Wertheim
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Unlike many art forms that take years to master, marbling offers instant gratification! In this workshop, Peggy will teach traditional marbling techniques using carrageenan and acrylic paints. You’ll create several marbled papers and a beautiful silk scarf. After the workshop, you can wear your new scarf and use your marbled papers for greeting cards, scrapbooking, collages, journal covers, and more. Just bring your love of art, creativity, and curiosity—everything else is provided.

item.title: Advanced Pattern Making In Kiln-Formed Glass: An Investigation Into Linear Symmetry With Ian Chadwick
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Symmetry can be used as a fundamental design tool. Symmetry is used by man and nature as a device to add continuity, balance and harmony to a chaotic universe, its use in art and design, consequently, attains an aesthetic of order and familiarity. In this five-day course, participants will explore principles of advanced pattern forming in fused glass. Using pre-formed Bullseye colored glass striped sheets, students will expand their knowledge and experience of kiln-forming and cold-working techniques to produce intricate patterns which utilize symmetry and geometry to create hypnotizing mandala-like patterns. Participants will be guided through the creation of Bullseye glass striped sheets which once fired will be deconstructed and reassembled. Participants will learn how the arrangement of tone and color can enhance the optical properties of the pattern design and how to lay out the pattern using principles of four-fold and eightfold symmetry. Students will utilize these concepts and techniques to create a circular 30cm diameter glass assemblage. We will also have an introduction to Ian's latest construction and hand coldworking method to finalize our workshop. All materials and firings included with this workshop. Closed toed shoes are required.  
This is an advanced workshop. Please email Carolyn@lighthousearts.org for more information and registration.

item.title: Alcohol Ink 3-Day Workshop with Alene Sirott Cope
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Alcohol ink is a dye/alcohol based ink that is fast drying, semi – transparent and can be used on non-porous surfaces.
  • Day 1: Intro - Create a colorful landscape on tile with alcohol onk while learning the basic technique. May be used for coasters, trivets, wall hanging, or on a table easel.
  • Day 2: Intermediate – Using the techniques from day 1 we will create backgrounds on “Yupo” paper to cut up and design collages with your own embellishments.
  • Day 3: Advanced- Learn the art of ‘masking’. Create a Saran Wrap background and mask with painters tape to reveal eye popping designs.

item.title: Looser Watercolors - Don't Work Too Hard! With Jeff Steiner
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This class focuses on four essential tools for creating strong, expressive watercolor paintings: color, shape, value, and edges. Through demonstrations and guided practice, students will learn how these elements work together to create depth, clarity, and energy. We will explore color by using warm and cool relationships to create mood and spatial depth. Shape will be simplified and connected to build clear, unified compositions. Value will be used to define form, volume, and light, giving structure to both urban and landscape scenes. Finally, we will work with edges, learning how to vary hard and soft transitions to create rhythm, focus, and movement. This class is designed to help students move beyond copying what they see and instead build paintings that feel organized, expressive, and dynamic — with confidence in their design choices and a deeper understanding of how watercolor works.

item.title: The Full Experience with Ron Shaw
item.dc:creator: Jlicata
item.content:encoded: In this Select Friday Event, students will experience the entire process of creating, glazing, and raku firing. The class begins with students glazing and loading the kiln with their complimentary vase, in preparation for the raku firing. Once the kiln is lit and heating, the wheel portion of the night begins. Students will learn to use the wheel to successfully create ceramic forms. They will be able to keep their best three creations of the night. After the wheel throwing, the red-hot kiln will be opened, and the glowing pots placed into combustion chambers, where the fire will create beautiful copper glaze results. All materials are provided.

item.title: Circles and More
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded:
Working with circles can be very challenging when it comes to glass. In this 4-week class students will learn how to carefully cut these curved shapes out of three different colors of glass. We will then cut them into various shapes and patterns. Using grinders and hand lap pads to smooth all the edges we will be able to reassemble them to create three beautiful round bowls. Students will then work with a rectangle shape to create a one-of-a-kind companion dish to compliment their bowls. Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this class. Additional materials and firing schedules are available for purchase. Please wear closed-toed shoes, comfortable clothes, and an apron.
Please email Carolyn with any questions at Carolyn@lighthousearts.org

item.title: Painting with Glass with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: sHinger

A special type of glass fusing paint that is used for drawing lines of your design on glass and them be able to shade on the glass with various colors to create detailed patterns between layers of glass to create complex dimensional effects in glass with fine tip applicators. You will be amazed at the effects you can achieve and come away with a decorative functional fused glass dish or bowl.
Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase. Please wear close-toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.

item.title: Reclaimed and Reimagined with Sandy Donabed
item.dc:creator: sHinger
item.content:encoded:
Explore ways of giving new life to fabric materials that have sentimental value, are part of your scrap pile, ripped apart, partially functional, something you inherited, etc. instead of adding to the landfills. Fiber art has a rich tradition of incorporating elements that would otherwise be discarded.
We will challenge ourselves to make art that incorporates recycled materials for your wall, table, or other living space. We will share ideas, trade fabrics, and encourage experimentation as we make a small art quilt-like piece that will explore techniques and cut right through those old ‘quilt-rules!’ Many examples will be included for developing new ideas.
We will concentrate on hand working traditions - embroidery, hand appliqué and quilting- and how to individualize stitching to each piece. So, no sewing machines are necessary.
This workshop is suitable for any level of sewer, artist, or quilter from beginner to professional.

item.title: Impact the Palm Beach: Private Select Fridays
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Acrylic Pouring

Bring your creative imagination to a fun new acrylic pouring workshop. We’ll explore how acrylics react to different mediums and substrates. You’ll be creating your own palettes, exploring how the pouring medium reacts to the acrylics as the medium continues to grow and react creating a vibrantly colored canvas or panel.

Shibori

Shibori is the ancient Japanese technique of creating patterns by binding, stitching, folding and twisting fabric during the dyeing process. Students will learn some basic traditional techniques such as Kumo and Itajime using commonly available commercial dyes. Students will experiment on a set of tea towels and are welcome to bring in additional items to dye. All items brought from home should be white or light colors. *Please dress expecting to get messy and wet. Bring a smock, over shirt or apron, and wear comfortable shoes.

Wheel Throwing

In this 2-hour Select Friday, students will gain the basic fundamentals of wheel work and a general understanding of the ceramic process, which includes firing & glazing. Each student will walk away having completed 4 pieces of their very own wheel thrown creation. All supplies included – no experience necessary.

Glass Fusion

Great for Beginners and a fun night out with friends and family! Try your hand at Glass Fusion. In this mini-workshop, you will learn how to assemble and properly lay out a pattern using a variety of colored glass, frit, and stingers to create a one-of-a-kind decorative sun catcher or coaster in a comfortable relaxed atmosphere.  Please wear closed-toed shoes, comfortable clothes, and an apron if you like.  All materials and firings included.

item.title: Exploring Cyanotype with Cathy Heeter
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
This two-day workshop is designed for the student who wants to learn about the cyanotype process, its unique history and explore its various applications. Students will be printing botanicals as well as other items on paper and fabric and will be learning how to achieve various results.
  • Day One: Students will print both wet and dry cyanotypes and experiment with adding additional materials to achieve a variety of results.
  • Day Two: Students will be doing additional printing and modifying prints from day one. Students will explore over dying, color removing, and toning.
Students can expect to leave with several finished pieces and ideas for how to incorporate cyanotype into their art practice.

item.dc:creator: dallen

“Art is Long, and life is short”- Hippocrates
Participants will learn the building blocks of painting while strengthening their artistic vision and skills. The essential use of drawing, mixing color and painting techniques are demonstrated in each class. Fundamentals using the notan sketch, limited palettes of color and color relationships, compositional elements like scale, ranging from big to small, structure in the rectangle and the use of the grid will be presented. Referencing images of great paintings from art history will guide our develop of ideas. Individuals are encouraged to explore their personal interests through experimentation and creativity! Beginners to painting are welcome.

item.title: Dilution Stacks in Fused Glass with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Create a beautiful glass bowl with stacked circles. Students will learn how surface tension and heat can produce perfect circles of glass without cutting a single curve. Learn how to cut and mix a variety of transparent colored glass with clear for a diluted look that will allow light to pass through and brighten the overall appearance of your glass art. After creating several different sizes of glass circle pebbles, we will determine the weight of stacks, lay out a glass pattern in the kiln with them to fuse again. Learn firing temperatures for all and preparation of molds for slumping will be the final phase of this session. This technique produces a beautiful, scalloped edge bowl for decorative and / or functional use!
Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase.
Please wear close-toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.

item.title: Fused Glass Mandalas with Stacy Gates
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Mandalas, which stands for circle, are created using symmetry, geometry and color patterns in a circular design. The Mandala is known to be a healing property, and the benefits of creating one includes: stress reduction, an alternative to meditation, exercise for the brain and one’s creativity. In this beginner friendly workshop, students will learn to cut glass properly to make consistent shapes; including circles, diamonds and triangles. They will also learn general design principles of mandalas and how to transfer your template and design onto glass.

item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Learning to draw begins with learning to see. In this class for adults, students will explore the fundamental difference between simply looking at something and truly seeing it. Through observational exercises, drawing line techniques, negative and positive space, and value gradation. We’ll slow down the process to train the eye and hand to work together. Students will develop their ability to perceive proportions, shapes, edges, and relationships more accurately laying the foundation for confident, expressive drawing. Whether you're a beginner or returning to drawing after a break, this class will sharpen your skills and deepen your understanding of visual perception. Suggested reading - Drawing on the Right side of the Brain by Betty Edwards is a great book to look at.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• Sketch book no larger than 9” x 12” (this is a sketch book that can be used in other classes)
  • Newsprint sketch book tape bound - 12” x 18” up to 18” x 24”
  • 1 Pad of Good Quality Drawing Paper (Strathmore 500 or equal) 12” x 9” up to 18” x 24”
  • Graphite Pencils {8B, 4B, 2B, HB, H}
  • Pack of Vine Charcoal – Soft and Medium (Thick or Medium Diameter)
  • Charcoal pencil Conte (Sanguine, Sepia and White)
  • Kneaded Rubber Eraser

item.title: Casting Extravaganza! with Gary Grossman
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This class is geared to safely experience many different metal casting techniques. You will be able to use your castings in Jewelry and/or small Metal Sculptures. Metal casting techniques will include Broom, Cuttlefish Bone, Tufa Stone, Sand, Natural objects, and Lost Wax. Each student will learn additive and reductive methods of working with various waxes as well as working with cuttle bone and tufa stone. Ancient bronze and sterling silver will be used for casting processes. Students are responsible for purchasing their own sterling silver casting grain. This class welcomes anyone curious about casting molten metal!

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: We will supply materials for the first day of class and go over the process of ordering your 1-2 oz. of sterling silver casting grain. You may use 50% solder free sterling silver scrap as part of your casting. Thus, please wait until class so we can explain. ;)

item.title: Guided Studio: Acrylic Painting with Caroline Duran
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This course serves as a guided studio to further develop an individual body of work. Students will explore acrylic painting skills while focusing on individual goals and subject matter. Skills focus on creating a successful composition, mixing observed values and colors based on selected reference photos, application of paint to canvas, and brushstroke techniques. The instructor will help guide each student in the planning and painting process from start to finish as needed. This course is accessible for all and individualized to meet each student’s skill level. Each student should bring a laptop or Ipad to each class to view their reference photo while painting.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• Acrylic Paint (primary colors/neutrals)
  • Plastic Pallet for mixing colors
  • Water Cup
  • Pencil
  • Eraser
  • Laptops for reference photos
  • 3-5 Stretched Canvas: 11 x 14 in. recommended
  • Paint brushes (various sizes)

item.title: Independent Jewelry Studio with Elia Gasbarro
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
This independent jewelry studio course is designed for experienced students who are ready to develop their own projects while working in a supportive studio environment. Participants must have foundational metalsmithing knowledge and be able to work independently. Students are expected to have prior experience with:
  • Bezel settings
  • Prong settings
  • Cold connections and soldered connections
  • Finishing techniques (filing, sanding, polishing, surface refinement)
  • Drilling techniques and proper tool use
  • Jeweler’s saw frame operation
  • Acetylene torch use and safety
This is not a beginner-level course. Students should feel confident setting up and executing their own projects from start to finish.
A studio monitor will be present to supervise the space, ensure safety compliance, and provide structured project prompts or creative challenges to support continued skill development. While instruction is not formal or step-by-step, guidance and technical feedback will be available as needed. This course is ideal for jewelers looking to refine their craftsmanship, expand technical ability, and build a cohesive body of work in a collaborative studio setting.

item.title: 3D Pattern Effects in Glass with Stacy Gates
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Step into the mesmerizing world of optical geometric precision! In this 4 week class, students will craft either a square or hexagon fused glass plate inspired by the eye-popping patterns of artists M.C. Escher and Victor Vasarely. Using an isometric grid as a foundation, you’ll explore the principles of perspective and visual perception to design a pattern that challenges the eye and tricks the mind. Students will learn to design on an isometric grid to create a 3D pattern effect by cutting glass into precise 60-degree diamonds. Cutting experience required. Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase.
Closed toed shoes required
Email Carolyn with any questions at: Carolyn@LighthouseArts.org

item.title: Endless Fused Glass Optics Techniques with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
In these 4-week classes you will learn to create a unique, optical look in fused glass. The basics of working with stringers and the art of cutting, grouping and laying out a specific pattern to complete a one-of-a-kind functional art glass project. There are many techniques and patterns that can be accomplished using stringers and Capz. We will use a variety of these by changing the Capz sizes and shape, parameters of glass and stringer sheets. Cold working skills will also be covered in these classes. Glass cutting skills recommended. Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase.
Closed toed shoes Required
Email Carolyn@LighthouseArts.org with any questions

item.title: Teen Portfolio Prep with Caroline Duran
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
This class is designed to guide motivated middle and high school students in the development and documentation of the 2D components in a well-rounded art portfolio.. The art portfolio is an important part of applications. Schools and universities want to gauge a student’s potential to be successful in courses belonging to your major of interest. Admissions teams want to know you as an artist in a way that goes beyond grades and test scores. They will take into consideration the level of instruction you’ve had, consider your portfolio, grades, difficulty of courses taken, recommendations, and application essay.  Successful artists and designers need to be creative thinkers. Creativity is often valued as much, if not more, than your technical skills as a developing artist.  Documentation is vital to presenting your artwork in a finished and professional light.  All artwork will be photographed with instructor assistance in preparation for a digital portfolio. 3D portfolio goals should be discussed with instructor/Lighthouse ArtCenter to gauge if we can accommodate the student’s individual needs on a private basis or in a separate course in the future.
In a portfolio, it is important to have breadth of knowledge and experimentation across mediums.
Topics that can be explored:
  • Still life
  • Grid Drawing
  • Painting (acrylic) – no oil painting unless water-mixable oil- no solvents or oils
  • Charcoal and Pastel
  • Color Pencil
  • representational vs. abstract work
  • conceptual vs. observational
Student Research (prior to start of class):
If you know what schools you want to apply to, research their portfolio requirements carefully and early. While researching the portfolio requirements of each school, pay particular attention to the following information:
  • Application and portfolio deadlines
  • How you need to submit your portfolio
  • If there are open days or portfolio days when you can present your portfolio in person
  • Number of pieces you should submit
  • Size requirements for the pieces
  • If there are any special required pieces you must submit (for example, the Rhode Island School of Design has required all applicants to submit a drawing of a bicycle)
  • You should also look at examples of previously submitted art portfolios.
Portfolio requirements often consist of the following:
  • Original artwork of the student's creation
  • 15-20 pieces showcasing various mediums, styles, and subjects
  • Demonstrate creativity, willingness to experiment, and critical thinking

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
Motivated Teens- grades 8-12
Prior art experience required

• Basic supplies are provided.  Students can bring in personal supplies if they prefer or if their project goals go beyond the scope of the provided materials.
  • Laptop, iPad, or phone needed for viewing reference images and documentation
  • Music will be played in the studio, but students can bring headphones to listen to personal music while working 
  • Water bottle (we are located in the Flex Space outside of the main gallery).

item.title: Butterfly Vase with Stacy Gates
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Let your creativity take flight in this fun workshop. You’ll design a colorful square inspired by monarch butterfly wings using sheet glass and a variety of glass frit. After a kiln firing, your piece will be draped over a stainless steel mold to become a flowing looking butterfly vase. Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase.
Closed toed shoes required
Email Carolyn with any questions at: Carolyn@LighthouseArts.org

item.title: Breaking Glass for Beginners with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Bring your creative ideas to this 2 week beginners glass class and learn the many possibilities of using a variety of colored glass, stringers and frit to create a one of a kind functional piece of art glass that you will be proud to use and display. Students will learn how to properly use the tools and materials required to assemble and lay out a design on glass along with the firing schedules to fuse and slump your glass project. Materials and firing schedules are supplied for this project with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase.
Closed toed shoes Required
Email Carolyn@lighthousearts.org with any questions

item.title: Botanical Art and Illustration with Eileen Lyons
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This 4 - week course will provide an exciting introduction to basic botanical illustration. Using pencil, ink and watercolor, participants will learn how to capture the beauty of the natural world. Through the use of photographs and direct observation, participant's will acquire skills in drawing and painting botanicals with realistic detail and expressive gestural composition.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: - Drawing Pad 9x12 inches - Watercolor pad 9x12 inches - Bristol board (optional) - Basic Watercolor paint box - Colored pencils - 2B pencil - Set of 3 microns

item.title: Art on the Floor with Lisa MacNamara
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Art on the Floor: Stand on Your Art, oh no! Create vibrant, functional art pieces designed to be walked on— an unexpected way to experience your own artwork!! In this hands-on workshop, you’ll design and paint a decorative floor covering on canvas, perfect for indoor or outdoor use. Learn techniques for binding, priming, and sealing your work for durability and even water resistance. Choose your size, from a smaller size, 24” x 12” for Fido’s water bowl or 3’x 5’ welcome home piece to make a statement- transform your art into a piece you can truly step into!
Please note: if you desire a bigger size, please contact me

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• Duck cloth canvas
  • Acrylic paints – even interior satin house paint works!
  • Your favorite image or designs
  • Your favorite repeating pattern – bring examples of patterns you like

item.title: Basic Drawing Skills with Eileen Lyons
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This 2-day workshop provides a solid foundation in drawing for the absolute beginner. With pencil, charcoal and conté, participants learn about line, value, composition, perspective and gestural sketching. Through fun observational exercises, participants will work on hand-eye coordination improving drawing skills. Subject matter will include still life, plant life, landscapes/seascapes, faces, architecture and perhaps some local birds, fish and shells. The workshop will include multiple demonstrations and discussion alternating with time for individual support and guidance.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:

  • Newsprint Pad 18 x 24 inches (any brand)
  • 2B, 4B, 8B Drawing Pencils (Graphite)
  • Basic Set of Conté Crayons
  • Vine Charcoal (Soft)
  • Kneaded Rubber Eraser
  • Blending Stumps
  • 2 Charcoal Pencils (one white, one black)

item.title: Art Clay Silver with Randi Berger
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Discover the magic of transforming clay into pure silver! No prior jewelry-making experience is required, just your creativity and curiosity.  Students will learn step-by-step techniques for working with Art Clay Silver, creating at least two unique pieces of wearable art. Through guided demonstrations, Randi will walk students through the four major stages of working with silver clay: Stage 1: Greenware (Wet Clay) - Explore tools, stamps, textures and molds while shaping your design. Learn how to incorporate a cubic zirconia gemstone and a dichroic glass cabochon for extra sparkle. Stage 2: Refining - Discover how to use files and sandpapers to refine your piece for a professional Jook. Stage 3: Firing -Learn about the different firing methods that transform the clay into silver. Stage 4: Finishing - Master polishing and patina techniques to highlight details and give your jewelry a beautiful, finished glow. By the end of this course, students will not only leave with their own handcrafted silver jewelry but also the foundations to continue exploring this versatile and rewarding art form.   Tuition includes 25grams of Art Clay Silver plus 10 grams of Syringe Clay

item.title: Paint Your Pet with Caroline Duran
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Come paint a portrait of your favorite furry friend. Students will how to trace an outline on canvas and how to mix/apply paints to achieve likeness. To participate, you must send photo of your pet to the instructor one week prior to the event at carolineduranart@outlook.com, along with the size of your canvas. This class is entry level, accessible for all, and no prior art experience is required. Join us to create a paw-fect masterpiece!

item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This course is accessible for levels from beginner to intermediate and is perfect for those seeking personal instruction. Guided studio allows each student to explore watercolor painting while focusing on individual goals and subject matter. Skills focus on mixing observed values and layering colors based on selected reference photos. The instructor will help guide each student in the planning and painting process from start to finish as needed.

item.title: Characters in Clay with Caroline Duran
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Learn how to create a sculpture that speak volumes! Sculptures may be based on people, animals, or imaginative characters. Skills that will be explored include solid/hollow building styles, modeling features, and glaze/underglaze best practices. This class is accessible for all experience levels from beginner to advanced!

item.title: The Art of Wire Wrapping with Cameron Walsh
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Students are introduced to wire wrapping techniques using essential tools such as pilers, clippers, and most importantly – their hands! Through guided instruction, demonstrations, and hands – on practice, students learn the styles of wire wrap jewelry. Students will learn how to create rings, pendants, and other wire wrapped jewelry items that include stones. This class is meant to offer students the knowledge and confidence to take on any wire wrap project with the proper comprehension and comfortability of a fine jewelry. Please wait until the class has been confirmed before ordering. The LAC will provide materials for the first day of class.

item.title: Abstracting Landscapes into Color Fields using Watercolor or Acrylic Paint with Lisa MacNamara
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this expressive class designed for adults of all skill levels, students will learn to deconstruct ocean landscapes into their essential shapes using watercolor’s fluid and spontaneous nature. Through guided exercises and personal exploration, participants will examine one landscape and transform it into abstract compositions, emphasizing line, color, and form rather than realistic details. This class encourages creative interpretation, helping students find their voice while deepening their understanding of abstraction and the expressive potential of watercolors and acrylics. All that is needed is a familiarity with the paints you want to use—just a willingness to loosen up and explore!

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: • Watercolor or Acrylic set of paints Watercolor pad of paper One 300 lb cold-press paper or canvas for the final painting

item.title: Fused Glass Wall Clocks with Stacy Gates
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Create a one of a kind wall clock out of glass. Students will learn the basics of fused glass art from cutting skills and design layout to how glass is formed in the kiln. Bring your creative ideas and and learn the many possibilities of using a variety of colored glass, stringers and frit to create a functional piece of art glass that you will be proud to display. Please wear closed toed shoes and an apron if you like. All materials and firings included with Additional materials and firing schedules available for purchase. Please wear closed toes shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.

item.title: Tricks with Transparency Glass with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Learn how to mix transparent colored glass with clear and other colors to allow light to pass through and create new colors and brighten the overall appearance of your glass art. Students will experiment with creating stacks of various colors of glass to transform manufactured glass into a challenging amazing one of a kind functional piece of glass art. Some cutting skills helpful. You will be sure to want to show off these beautiful pieces of art glass you create in this 4 week session!
All materials and firing schedules included with additional materials and firings available for purchase. Please wear closed toed shoes, comfortable clothes and an apron.

item.title: Wrapped Ring with a Stone with Cameron Walsh
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this workshop, students learn the fundamentals of wire wrap using essential tools such as pliers, clippers, and their hands. Through guided instruction and hands-on practice, participants design and create a sterling silver ring featuring a gemstone. From shaping and wrapping the band to setting the stone and polishing the final piece, each student leaves with a handcrafted, personally designed ring and a deeper appreciation for the Art of Wire Wrap.

item.title: Fused Glass Recipe Plate or Spoon Rest with Carolyn Austin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Create a beautiful Recipe Plate or Spoon Rest in fused glass. Students will learn the basics of glass fusion to design and create a one of a kind functional piece of glass art. Bring a special -short- Recipe in your handwriting to copy on glass with Glassline paints. Overall glass size will be 7" x 9"
This is a great Mother's Day Gift. All materials and firings included with additional available for purchase.
Closed toed shoes required. Please email Carolyn@lighthousearts.org with any questions or send your recipe for approval of size to fit on glass.

item.title: Textured Pendant with a Bezel Cup
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Students will learn how to apply texture to nonferrous metal using a variety of different hammers to produce a unique surface for a pendant. To spice it up, each student will learn how to solder a bezel cup and set a stone to complete their beautiful pendant/charm.

item.title: Intermediate Drawing - The Portrait with Lisa MacNamara
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
This seven-week course deconstructs the human face, focusing on each individual element before thoughtfully reconstructing the portrait as a whole. Through careful observation and analysis, students gain a deeper understanding of facial structure, proportion, and relationships that inform expressive and accurate portrait drawing.
In this skill-building class, students expand their drawing abilities through a series of focused observational exercises centered on the human face. Working with line, shape, proportion, and value, students develop stronger visual accuracy while deepening their understanding of how to translate what they see onto the page. Emphasis is placed on seeing beyond symbols to observe structure, relationships, and subtle variations unique to each portrait.
Throughout the course, students will learn to:
  • Refine line quality through varied drawing techniques
  • Analyze and apply positive and negative space
  • Build value gradations to create depth, form, and likeness
  • Improve perception of proportions, shapes, edges, and spatial relationships
  • Strengthen observational confidence to create more expressive and intentional portraits
    Drawing experience suggested

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• Sketch book no larger than 9” x 12” (this is a sketch book that can be used in other classes)
  • Newsprint sketch book tape bound - 12” x 18” up to 18” x 24”
  • 1 Pad of Good Quality Drawing Paper (Strathmore 500 or equal) 12” x 9” up to 18” x 24”
  • Graphite Pencils {8B, 4B, 2B, HB, H}
  • Pack of Vine Charcoal – Soft and Medium (Thick or Medium Diameter)
  • Charcoal pencil Conte (Sanguine, Sepia and White)
  • Kneaded Rubber Eraser Small watercolor set

item.title: Sculpture with Character Through Caricature: The Art of Portraiture, My Way with Chris Riccardo
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this hands on 3-Day Workshop, learn to create portrait sculptures that capture more than a face—they reveal a soul. In this immersive weekend intensive, you'll master Chris Riccardo's proven approach to sculpture with character through caricature. Discover how strategic observation and fearless distortion combine to create portraits that are more truthful than realism alone could ever be. This isn't about copying faces. It's about interpreting personality, amplifying essence, and sculpting with confidence and artistic courage.

item.title: From Flat to Form: The Joy of Building with Slabs with Jen Allen
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Join Jen for a lively two-day workshop that turns simple slabs into dynamic, dimensional pots. Through engaging demos, Jen will share her favorite ways to build texture with handmade stamps, inflate and alter slabs, and transform quick clay sketches into dependable templates.
You’ll also get a short hands-on session to play with Jen’s Pottery Patterns (template sets) and try out key techniques like darting - without the pressure to make finished work.
Whether you’re a handbuilder or thrower, you’ll head home with fresh ideas, practical tools, and a renewed excitement to explore what’s possible with clay.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
General
  • Sketchbook + pencil – For notes and design ideas
  • Curiosity and patience – Essential studio tools!
Clay Tools
  • Rubber rib(s)
  • Needle/pin tool
  • X-Acto knife (dull preferred – sharp ones cut hands and canvas!) or Dolan knife. Fettling knife or pairing knife will work but not ideal.
  • Rolling pin or dowel
  • Serrated rib
  • Square-end trimming tools (for making clay strips) optional
  • Brush or ball point stylus – For smoothing seams and surfaces
Other Equipment Banding wheel, turntable, or lazy Susan – Free-spinning preferred

item.title: Carving Out A Painting with Beth Bathe
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Reductive painting technique using water mixable oil paint and limited tonal palette

Wondering what Water Mixable Oil paints are all about? Known for blurring the line between watercolor and oil paintings, Beth Bathe's unparalleled style evokes feelings of nostalgia, like an old sepia-toned photograph. Beth uses unconventional tools including squeegees and cotton swabs, along with her brushes focusing on composition, values, edges, and drawing rather than color.

During this 2 day intensive studio workshop, Beth shares her unique technique with students. In the mornings Beth will do a demo and show how she uses photography and simple apps on her phone to simplify forms enhance value and emphasize composition. In the afternoon students will work from photos (either bring your own on your phone/iPad, or Beth will have prints to share).

Students are encouraged to use water mixable oils to get the most out of the workshop. Beth will have paint for her students to try as well as one of her prepared painting panels, brushes and other supplies for you to use during the workshop.

Workshop could be for beginners through advanced. Beth will not be teaching the fundamentals of oil painting (color mixing theory etc), rather her technique with just one or two colors. Students who have previously taken a class with Beth are also encouraged to attend.

Studio Workshop

Day 1 - Morning: introduction, hand out supplies and demo by Beth.  Afternoon: students will set up on easels and Beth will provide individual instruction to students. Students may gesso their boards for day 2/3 Beth will offer her demos for sale.

Day 2  –  Morning critique of paintings painted from day prior Beth will set up and start a demo.  Each day demo will focus on different subject matter and Break for lunch. Afternoon will be students painting on their own with personal instruction. Last day, last half hour we will have a group critique and wrap up. Beth will offer her demos for sale.

Other incidental costs for students:

Demo paintings will be available for purchase from workshop attendees for $400 (payable to Beth Bathe via cash, check or Venmo)

Additional painting panels and paint brushes may be available to purchase from Beth

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
Beth Bathe Supply List:

Beth will be providing (extra $60 fee per student)

• One prepared hardboard panel for students to use(for day one), additional panels(for day two and three) must be purchased by students (see below)

• Use of Beth’s Cobra water mixable oils. She will squeeze paint onto individual paper plates for you to use.

• Three paint brushes (that student can keep)

• squeegees (2)

• Q-tips • photo reference materials to use (or you may bring your own prints or ipad). She will also show you how she makes composition decisions using apps you have on your phone.

 

What student needs to bring to class:

• Painting panel(s) for day 2, Beth recommends acylic pre-gessoed hardboards such as Ampersand Gessobords and Richeson hardboard flat panels(which you would need to gesso) 9x12 or larger, one per day plus extras if you want. Beth recommends trying different sizes. Beth will have extra gesso that students may use to prepare their panels..

• Roll of bounty paper towels, palette or palette or Beth will have paper plates you can use

• Trash bag (like a plastic grocery bag)

• container for water (to use to paint and clean brushes)

• Apron (recommended)

• reference photos. Either a print or your phone or iPad will also work. Beth will also have photo printouts you can borrow of subject matter that is appropriate for the class

• Bag Lunch or students my order lunch from one of the nearby restaurants

item.title: Clay Fairy Houses: For the Garden or Home with Zoe Lowenthal
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In this fun hands-on, 2-day workshop, students will create whimsical fairy houses. First, with instructor and individual guidance using handbuilding techniques like slab construction and decorative attachments, each student will complete a unique fairy house of their own. On the second day, the group will bring their creations to life by painting them with underglaze. Clay, underglaze and most studio tools will be provided.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Sketchbook, writing device, and any personal clay tools.

item.title: Customize Your Life: Ceramic Mug or Stein with Zoe Lowenthal
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: In just 2 hours, students will design and construct a custom mug/stein using slab techniques. Each student will learning how to shape a cylinder and attach key elements like a handle and base. After the main construction is complete students are able and highly encourage to bring their unique style to the surface decoration. Ultimately, make a fun mug/stein you are proud of and look forward to using. All materials are provided.

item.title: Sound Objects & Whistling Vessels with Patricia Reagan
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: This adult ceramic course explores clay through the creation of sound-producing objects inspired by Pre-Columbian traditions. Each session introduces a new sonic form, increasing in complexity as students build technical skill and confidence. Along the way, participants learn how ancient cultures understood sound, breath, and water as sacred elements. The course culminates in the creation of a functional whistling vessel.

item.title: Masters' Finishing Workshop with Eduardo Gomez
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Designed for students with bisque-fired clay pieces, this 2-Day workshop offers hands-on guidance to bring each sculpture to a fully finished state.(no more firings) Whether applying a "cold finish" / "patina" for the first time or refining an existing surface, participants will receive both technical instruction and aesthetic insight to help determine the best approach for their work.
Participants are welcome to bring multiple pieces and use all materials while they are available.

item.title: Intro to Sgraffito with Renee Schwaller
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Take your ceramic surface decoration to new heights with Sgraffito. Sgraffito, an Italian word meaning “to scratch”, is an ancient pottery technique involving carving through a top layer of slip to reveal a contrasting colored clay beneath. In this workshop, Renee will teach you how she uses this technique with underglazes, to adorn her pots and tiles.  The workshop will begin with a short slide presentation, a demonstration and then the students will practice this  technique with a leather hard pot they have supplied or a tile, which will be on hand for them.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: -One to two forms that are leather hard ready for carving during Workshop.  -Personal carving tools. - inspirational imagery for carving.

item.title: Jewelry Fabrication & Stone Setting with Joel Schwalb
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: The objective of this class is to become proficient in several different stone setting techniques including bezel setting prong setting and flush setting. We will accomplish this by designing and fabricating several pieces such as a pendant bracelet earrings etc. We will be working with silver brass copper your choice. We will review different fabrication techniques. Previous experience using a torch is necessary. You will be expected to provide any stones that you want to include in the piece that you will be fabricating.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
• Silver, brass or copper sheet 3 inches by 4 inches
  • silver ,brass or copper wire 22 or 24 Gage

item.title: Fold Forming Workshop with Joel Schwalb
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Learn how to make pins pendants bracelets etc using this technique called Fold forming. We will be using 24 Gage copper sheet metal in this workshop to learn this unique technique it involves folding hammering along the fold line and then opening three fold refolding on another access hammering again and reopening to the second fold. Many interesting forms can be created using this method. I will be demonstrating these techniques to you then you will proceed with my guidance I will also demonstrate methods of coloring the copper using a torch and also using chemical patinas this workshop is open to all levels of experiences and materials will be provided.

item.title: Open Sewing Studio with Camile Perrin
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded: Love to sew? Want to expand your artistic and technical skills? We will explore improvisational quilting, piecing, applique ,collage, color theory, textures, embellishments and more. Bring your machine, your sewing tools , current projects , your ideas and any designs you would like to develop . This is the perfect class for anyone who wants to add some fun techniques to their sewing skills.! Basic machine sewing skills are preferred.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Sewing machine in good working order, basic sewing tools, fabrics etc. Current projects, ideas etc.

item.title: Shark Tooth Ring with Elia Gasbarro
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
Students will learn how to create a handcrafted ring inspired by natural forms, focusing on shaping and refining an organic, sculptural design. The objective is to guide participants through the process of transforming raw materials into a finished, wearable piece.
This class introduces foundational jewelry techniques including forming, soldering, and surface finishing. Emphasis is placed on achieving an organic texture and unique shape, allowing each ring to feel one of a kind.
The course is structured as a step-by-step, hands- on workshop suitable for beginners and intermediate students. All materials and tools are provided, and students will leave with a completed ring by the end of the session.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Students can bring their own shark tooth or the teacher can supply them with one. All other material will be supplied by the studio.

item.title: Cowrie Ring with Elia Gasbarro
item.dc:creator: dallen
item.content:encoded:
This course introduces students to creating a bezel- set shell ring, focusing on foundational metalsmithing skills while completing a polished, wearable piece within a single session. Students will build confidence by working with metal and leaving with a unique, coastal- inspired ring. Students will work with pre-made ring bands and bezel settings, allowing them to focus on essential techniques such as soldering components together, refining surfaces through filing and sanding, and securely setting a shell. Emphasis is placed on proper torch use, clean solder joins, and achieving a smooth finish. All materials are provided for students. This three-hour class is a beginner- friendly and guided step-by-step, ensuring each student successfully completes their ring.
Level Beginner
Price Member $100 Non Member $110
